CONTENT-PROMPTS.title: CONTENT-PROMPTS
CONTENT-PROMPTS.content:
# Content prompts

Copy-paste prompts for extending this site without it drifting in voice or
accuracy. Each one is written to be pasted into Claude Code from the repo root,
so the model can read the actual code rather than inventing behaviour.

---

## The house style, in one paragraph

Paste this at the top of any content prompt so new pages match the existing ones.

Write in RetAI documentation voice: direct, second person, no marketing
> adjectives. Short paragraphs. Lead with what the reader does, then why it
> behaves that way. State limitations plainly — a published constraint is more
> credible than an omission. Use `` for context, `` for the thing
> experienced users know, and `` only where the consequence is real
> (data loss, money, a message to a patient, a legal obligation). Never write a
> claim you have not verified in the code. Indian market: ₹, GST, DPDP, WhatsApp
> as the primary channel. No em-dashes-as-drama, no "simply", no "just", no
> "seamlessly", no "empower".

---

## 1. Add a page for a new module

```
Read src/app/(dashboard)// and src/lib// in full.

Write docs-site/features/.mdx documenting it, matching the structure and
voice of docs-site/features/packages.mdx exactly:

- YAML frontmatter: title, description, icon (Font Awesome 6 free name)
- One  screenshot near the top with a caption
- What the module is for, in two sentences, before any UI detail
-  for the primary task
- A table for fields, statuses, or options
-  for secondary detail
- At least one  covering a real consequence
- A "Related"  at the end

Document only behaviour you can point to in the code. Where the code has a
known limitation, say so in the page rather than omitting it.

Then add the page to docs.json under the Modules group, in sidebar order.
Finally, add any screenshots it references to docs-site/SCREENSHOTS.md with
capture instructions in the same format as the existing entries.
```

---

## 2. Verify a page against the code

Run this on every page before publishing. It is the single highest-value prompt here.

```
Read docs-site/.mdx.

For every factual claim it makes about product behaviour, find the code that
implements it. Report a table:

| Claim | File:line that supports it | Verdict |

Verdict is one of: CONFIRMED, CONTRADICTED, NOT FOUND.

Do not fix anything. Do not assume a feature exists because it would be
reasonable. If you cannot find the code, say NOT FOUND.
```

---

## 3. Document an API endpoint accurately

```
Read src/app/api//route.ts in full, including its imports.

Write the endpoint section for docs-site/api-reference/endpoints/.mdx:

- Method and path
-  for every parameter the handler actually reads — no invented filters
-  for the real response shape, including nullability
- A curl example
- The exact status codes this handler can return, and why
- Any side effect the write triggers (queued message, stock deduction, calendar push)
- Its rate limit, if src/lib/rate-limit.ts covers it

Where the handler resolves clinic scope server-side, say so — that is a security
property worth documenting, not an implementation detail.
```

---

## 4. Write a workflow walkthrough

```
Write docs-site/workflows/.mdx for the task: .

Match docs-site/workflows/consultation-to-invoice.mdx in structure and voice.

Rules:
- One  block, each  a single action the reader takes
- Name the actual screen and button at each step
- After the steps, a table of what happens automatically afterwards
- Call out the one step people skip when busy, and why it matters most
- End with a "Related" CardGroup

Read the relevant code under src/app/(dashboard)/ first. Every screen and button
you name must exist.
```

---

## 5. Turn a support question into a docs entry

Use this whenever the same question reaches support twice.

```
A clinic asked: ""

Answer it from the code, then:
1. Add it to docs-site/help/faq.mdx under the right heading, as an 
2. If it is a failure with a fix, add it to docs-site/help/troubleshooting.mdx
   instead, in the format: cause in one sentence, then **Fix:**, then
   **Prevent:** where prevention is possible
3. If it reveals a genuinely missing page, say so and propose the page

Keep it under 120 words. If the honest answer is "the product does not do
that", write that.
```

---

## 6. Refresh the changelog for a release

```
Read the git log since .

Add an  block at the top of docs-site/help/changelog.mdx:
- label: the month
- description: a 2-4 word release theme
- H2 per user-visible change, with a short paragraph on what it means in the clinic
- Group small changes under a bold "Also in this release" list
- If anything corrects a previously wrong behaviour (a tax calculation, a
  permission), include a  telling clinics what to re-check

Skip internal refactors, dependency bumps, and test-only changes. If a change
is not visible to a clinic, it does not belong here.
```

---

## 7. Adapt the docs for a new specialty

```
This documentation is written for dermatology and aesthetic clinics. Produce a
variant for .

For each page under docs-site/features/ and docs-site/workflows/, list:
- What stays identical
- What needs different examples (services, packages, clinical terms)
- What is irrelevant and should be cut
- What the new specialty needs that is not documented at all

Do not write the pages yet. Produce the plan first, as a table.
```

---

## 8. Generate the landing-site copy from these docs

```
Read docs-site/index.mdx, features/overview.mdx, features/chats.mdx,
features/at-risk.mdx, and features/packages.mdx.

Write landing-page copy for www.retai.tech/product, structured like a
competitor product page: one section per feature cluster, each with a heading,
a one-line promise, and 4-6 short sub-features.

Constraints:
- Every claim must be traceable to something in these docs
- No outcome promises ("increase revenue by 40%")
- No claim about competitors
- Indian market: ₹, GST, WhatsApp, DPDP
- Marketing register is allowed, invention is not

End each section with a link to the matching docs page.
```

---

## 9. Write alt text for every screenshot

Do this once, after capture. It matters for accessibility and for SEO.

```
For every  in docs-site/**/*.mdx, the alt attribute currently repeats the
caption. Rewrite each one to describe what is visually in the image for someone
who cannot see it — the screen, the key elements, and the state being
demonstrated. Under 125 characters each.

Output as a list of file, current alt, proposed alt. Do not edit yet.
```

---

## 10. Pre-publish audit

Run this last, before pointing the domain at the site.

```
Audit docs-site/ for publication readiness. Report only problems, as a table of
file, issue, severity:

1. Any placeholder left: XXXXXXXX, TODO, TBD, [brackets], lorem, example.com
2. Any phone number, email, or URL that is not RetAI's own
3. Any internal detail that should not be public: env var names, table names,
   internal file paths, vendor pricing
4. Any claim about security, uptime, compliance, or data handling that is
   stated more strongly than docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/legal/ support
5. Any broken internal link
6. Any referenced image file that does not exist
7. Voice inconsistency against docs-site/features/packages.mdx

Do not fix anything. Report only.
```

---

## Two prompts to avoid

**"Write documentation for this product."** Produces plausible fiction. The
model will invent screens that do not exist and features that sound reasonable.
Always scope a prompt to specific files it must read first.

**"Make this sound more professional."** Produces marketing mush and strips out
exactly the specific, verifiable detail that makes the site trustworthy. If a
page reads badly, say what is wrong with it.

README.content:
# RetAI documentation site (Mintlify)

Public product documentation for RetAI / RetAI, built with [Mintlify](https://mintlify.com).

Lives on the `docs-site` branch, in this `docs-site/` directory, deliberately separate from
the application so docs deploys never touch the app.

Not to be confused with `/docs` at the repo root — that is internal engineering
documentation (architecture, audits, legal drafts) and stays private.

---

## Run it locally

```bash
npm i -g mint
```

```bash
cd docs-site && mint dev
```

Opens on http://localhost:3000. Hot-reloads on save.

Check every link before shipping:

```bash
cd docs-site && mint broken-links
```

---

## Structure

```
docs-site/
├── docs.json                    # Site config: theme, colors, nav, footer, SEO
├── index.mdx                    # Home
├── quickstart.mdx
├── onboarding.mdx               # The 10-step rollout programme
├── concepts.mdx
├── workflows/                   # Task-oriented walkthroughs
├── features/                    # One page per product module
├── admin/                       # Setup and configuration
│   └── integrations/
├── security/                    # Security & Trust tab
├── api-reference/               # API tab
│   ├── endpoints/
│   └── webhooks/
├── help/                        # FAQ, troubleshooting, support, changelog
├── logo/                        # light.svg, dark.svg
├── images/                      # Screenshots — see SCREENSHOTS.md
└── snippets/                    # Reusable MDX fragments
```

Three tabs: **Documentation**, **Security & Trust**, **API Reference**.

---

## Before you publish

Two checklists, both mandatory:

- **`SCREENSHOTS.md`** — every image the site references, with the exact filename,
  what to capture, and the demo data to use. Pages render without them, but with
  broken image slots.
- **`REVIEW-BEFORE-PUBLISH.md`** — placeholders and unverified claims that must be
  confirmed before this goes public. Several are legal or compliance statements.

---

## Deploying

1. Sign in at [mintlify.com](https://mintlify.com) with GitHub
2. Connect this repository
3. Set the content directory to `docs-site`
4. Set the deployment branch (`docs-site` while drafting, `main` once merged)
5. Add the custom domain `docs.retai.tech` and create the CNAME Mintlify gives you

Every push to the configured branch redeploys.

---

## Editing conventions

- **One page per module.** If a page needs two H1-level ideas, it is two pages.
- **State limitations.** Known constraints are published, not hidden. It is the
  most credible thing on the site — see `security/architecture.mdx`.
- **Warnings are for real consequences.** Overuse makes them invisible.
- **Never write a claim you have not verified in the code.** This site is read by
  clinics evaluating whether to trust us with patient data.
- **No real patient data in screenshots, ever.** Demo tenant only.

REVIEW-BEFORE-PUBLISH.title: REVIEW-BEFORE-PUBLISH
REVIEW-BEFORE-PUBLISH.content:
# Review before publishing

This site is read by clinics deciding whether to trust you with patient data,
and by their lawyers. Everything below is either a placeholder, an unverified
claim, or a feature described in the docs that may not exist in the product yet.

**Work through all four sections before pointing `docs.retai.tech` at this.**

---

## 1. Placeholders that will embarrass you

| File | Line item | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs.json` | `integrations.ga4.measurementId: "G-XXXXXXXXXX"` | Real GA4 ID, or delete the `integrations` block |
| `docs.json` | `footer.socials` — LinkedIn and X URLs | Confirm they exist, or remove |
| `docs.json` | `navbar.links` → `status.retai.tech` | The status page must exist. It is linked from six pages. If there is no status page, remove every link to it. |
| `docs.json` | `logo`, `favicon` | Placeholder SVGs are committed. Replace with the real mark. |
| `docs.json` | `seo.metatags["og:image"]` | Create `images/og-cover.png` |
| `docs.json` | Global anchor → `wa.me/919108729324` | **This is Cliniceo's support number, used as a structural placeholder. Replace it with yours before publishing.** |
| Multiple | `support@retai.tech`, `security@retai.tech` | Both must be real, monitored mailboxes. `security@` is published as a vulnerability-report address with a one-business-day acknowledgement commitment. |
| `index.mdx`, `onboarding.mdx` | `https://www.retai.tech/pricing`, `/support` | Confirm these pages exist on the landing site |

---

## 2. Legal and compliance — needs a lawyer, not a developer

The source documents in `/docs/legal/` are marked **DRAFT — pending review by a
qualified Indian lawyer**. The docs site restates parts of them.

| Claim | Where | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 99.5% monthly uptime target | `security/sla.mdx` | **Confirm you can stand behind this given Vercel's and Supabase's own SLAs.** Do not commit publicly to more than your infrastructure guarantees you. |
| Support response times (1h / 4h / 1d / 3d) | `security/sla.mdx`, `help/support.mdx` | Confirm these are operationally achievable. A published 1-hour critical response you cannot meet is a contractual problem. |
| Service credit percentages | `security/sla.mdx` | Legal review |
| 30-day export window, 30-day deletion, 90-day backup purge | `security/retention-and-deletion.mdx` | Verify against actual Supabase backup configuration. The source policy has these in `[brackets]` as placeholders. |
| Audit log retained 3 years minimum | `security/retention-and-deletion.mdx` | Verify against actual retention configuration |
| Access logs retained 12 months | `security/retention-and-deletion.mdx` | Verify |
| 15 business days to action a deletion instruction | `security/dpdp.mdx` | Legal review |
| 15 days' notice before a new subprocessor | `security/dpdp.mdx`, `security/subprocessors.mdx` | Must match the executed DPA |
| Bolna hosting region shown as "Confirm" | `security/subprocessors.mdx` | **Get the real answer from Bolna and state it.** A subprocessor table with "Confirm" in it looks worse than an unflattering true answer. |
| Supabase region "selected at project setup" | `security/subprocessors.mdx` | State the actual region |
| "Not HIPAA compliant, no BAAs" | `security/overview.mdx`, `subprocessors.mdx`, `help/faq.mdx` | Accurate today. Revisit if BAAs are ever executed. |



**A note on the honesty in these pages.** Several published limitations —
non-atomic invoice writes, per-instance rate limiting, backup rotation delay —
came out of your own audit. Publishing them is a deliberate trust play and it is
the most credible content on the site. Do not let a reviewer quietly delete
them; if any one is fixed, update the page rather than removing the section.

---

## 3. Features documented that may not exist yet

Written from the code, the architecture map, and the derma feature spec. Some
spec items are Stage 3–4 and not built. **Verify each against the running app;
delete or mark as "coming soon" anything that is not there.**

| Feature | Documented in | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scheduled reports by email/WhatsApp | `features/reports.mdx` | Does the scheduler exist? |
| Vendors and purchase orders | `features/inventory.mdx` | Spec says missing as of the gap analysis |
| Prescription fulfilment against stock | `features/inventory.mdx`, `features/consultations.mdx` | Spec says missing |
| Stock take with variance posting | `features/inventory.mdx` | |
| Patient merge | `features/patients.mdx` | |
| Feedback capture and analytics | `features/reports.mdx` | Spec says missing |
| Incentive payout report | `features/reports.mdx` | Spec says missing |
| Demographics report | `features/reports.mdx` | Spec says missing |
| Quotation builder and PDF | `features/leads.mdx`, workflows | Spec lists counselling/quotations as missing entirely |
| Retainer and clinic credit | `features/billing.mdx` | Spec says missing |
| Photo collections | `features/gallery.mdx` | |
| Multi-location clinic switching | `concepts.mdx`, `help/faq.mdx` | |
| Recording consent announcement | `admin/integrations/voice.mdx` | Confirm Bolna supports it as described |
| Configurable image retention | `admin/clinic-setup.mdx` | |
| Full clinic export as a background job with a link | `admin/data-export.mdx` | Verify it is not a synchronous download |
| API query params on every endpoint | `api-reference/endpoints/*` | **Verify each parameter name against the actual route handlers.** These were written from the architecture map, which lists routes and methods but not every filter. |
| `source` field on appointments (`ai_whatsapp` etc.) | `api-reference/endpoints/appointments.mdx` | Confirm the field and its values |
| `at_risk_score` on the patient response | `api-reference/endpoints/patients.mdx` | Confirm it is exposed |



> **The cheapest way to do this section:** open the running app next to each
> page and click through it. Anything you cannot find in two minutes, a
> prospective customer will not find either.

---

## 4. Content and consistency

- [ ] All 35 screenshots captured — see `SCREENSHOTS.md`
- [ ] `mint broken-links` passes clean
- [ ] Product naming settled. The code uses **RetAI** (logo, architecture doc) and **RetAI** (README, package name, domain). This site treats RetAI as the company and RetAI as the product. **Confirm that is what you want, then make it consistent everywhere including the landing site.**
- [ ] The AI agent is called **Aisha** throughout. Confirm that is the shipping name.
- [ ] Currency shown as ₹ throughout — correct for the Indian market
- [ ] `help/changelog.mdx` dates match the actual release history
- [ ] `security/subprocessors.mdx` change-history table has a real first row
- [ ] The `docs.json` banner text is current (it announces WhatsApp booking)
- [ ] Read `index.mdx` and `quickstart.mdx` aloud. They are the two pages everyone reads.

---

## 5. Final gate

- [ ] No real patient data in any screenshot
- [ ] No secret, key, or token visible anywhere
- [ ] Legal pages reviewed by an Indian lawyer
- [ ] SLA numbers you can actually meet
- [ ] Every documented feature exists, or is marked as coming
- [ ] Someone other than the author has read the whole site

SCREENSHOTS.title: SCREENSHOTS
SCREENSHOTS.content:
# Screenshot capture checklist

35 images. Every path below is already referenced by a page — save each file at
exactly the path shown and it appears automatically.

---

## Ground rules — read before capturing anything

1. **Demo tenant only. Never a live clinic.** These pages go public. A real
   patient name in a screenshot is a data breach, not a typo.
2. **Use the demo patient set below** across every shot. The same names
   recurring makes the docs feel like one product instead of thirty unrelated
   screens.
3. **Browser: 1440 × 900, dark theme, 2× DPI.** The site's default appearance is
   dark and the app is dark-first. Retina export keeps text sharp.
4. **Hide browser chrome.** No URL bar, no bookmarks, no extensions, no OS clock.
   Capture the app viewport only.
5. **Populate the data first.** An empty calendar or a two-row patient list makes
   the product look unfinished. Every screen wants realistic density.
6. **PNG. Under 500 KB each.** Run everything through an optimiser before commit.
7. **Crop tight** to the region the caption talks about. A full-page screenshot
   where the caption discusses one panel wastes the reader's attention.

### Demo data set — use these everywhere

| Patients | Clinicians | Services |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Priya Sharma · Ananya Rao · Meghna Iyer | Dr Meera Iyer | Laser hair reduction — full legs (₹8,000, 45 min) |
| Rohan Desai · Kavya Nair · Aditi Menon | Dr Arjun Kapoor | HydraFacial (₹4,500, 60 min) |
| Sneha Pillai · Vikram Shetty | Dr Sana Qureshi | Chemical peel (₹3,500, 30 min) |
| Divya Krishnan · Nikhil Raman | | Acne consultation (₹800, 20 min) |
| | | PRP — scalp (₹12,000, 60 min) |

Phone numbers: `+9198765 4321x`. Clinic: **Lumière Skin & Hair, Bengaluru**.

---

## Home — 1 image

### `images/hero-dashboard.png`
**Screen:** Overview dashboard, signed in as owner
**Shows:** Revenue-recovered figure, at-risk count, today's appointment list, recent activity
**Set up:** Populate a month of history so charts have a real curve. Revenue recovered should show a non-trivial number — this is the first thing a prospect sees.
**Crop:** Full dashboard viewport
**Caption already written:** "The RetAI overview dashboard — revenue recovered, at-risk patients, and today's schedule on one screen."

---

## Quickstart — 4 images

### `images/quickstart/01-login.png`
**Screen:** `/login`
**Shows:** Clinic branding, Google sign-in button, email/password fields
**Set up:** Clean state, nothing typed, no error banner

### `images/quickstart/02-staff.png`
**Screen:** CRM → Staff
**Shows:** 5–6 staff members across all three roles, with the module permission matrix visible
**Set up:** At least one receptionist with a non-default toggle, so the matrix looks used rather than pristine

### `images/quickstart/03-calendar.png`
**Screen:** Calendar, day view
**Shows:** Three clinician columns, 10–14 appointments, a mix of statuses including at least one amber tentative
**Set up:** A realistic clinic day — busy morning, quieter afternoon, a lunch gap

### `images/quickstart/04-ai-draft.png`
**Screen:** At-Risk → Draft message modal
**Shows:** The generated message with the patient's context panel beside it
**Set up:** Priya Sharma, 3 of 6 laser sessions remaining, 9 weeks since last visit. Draft must read naturally — regenerate until it does.

---

## Modules — 20 images

### `images/features/calendar-day-view.png`
**Screen:** Calendar, day view
**Shows:** Resource columns per clinician, colour-coded statuses, live current-time line
**Crop:** 09:00–18:00 so the whole working day is visible

### `images/features/calendar-ai-booking.png`
**Screen:** Appointment detail for an AI-created booking
**Shows:** The appointment panel with its conversation origin visible — that it came from WhatsApp is the entire point of the shot
**Set up:** Book one through the demo WhatsApp flow so it is genuine

### `images/features/patient-profile.png`
**Screen:** Patients → Priya Sharma
**Shows:** Overview tab with history, active package, recent invoices, conversation preview, and a clinical flag pinned at top
**Set up:** Give her a full history — 9 visits, an allergy flag, one active package

### `images/features/at-risk-list.png`
**Screen:** At-Risk Patients
**Shows:** 8–10 rows sorted by revenue at stake, each with its stated reason and value
**Set up:** Vary the reasons — sessions remaining, long gap, expiring package, recent no-show. The variety is what shows the score is doing work.

### `images/features/at-risk-ai-draft.png`
**Screen:** At-Risk → Draft message, expanded
**Shows:** Draft alongside the grounding context the model was given
**Note:** Different crop from `quickstart/04` — this one emphasises the grounding panel

### `images/features/revenue-recovered-chart.png`
**Screen:** Reports → Revenue recovered
**Shows:** 6-month trend with attribution to outreach
**Set up:** An upward but not absurd curve. A hockey stick reads as fake.

### `images/features/whatsapp-inbox.png`
**Screen:** WhatsApp Inbox
**Shows:** Thread list on the left with unread badges and one **Needs attention** flag; an open conversation on the right with patient context beside it
**Set up:** The open thread should show a real exchange — patient asks about a treatment, Aisha answers, patient asks for a slot, Aisha offers times. 6–8 messages.

### `images/features/receptionist-call-log.png`
**Screen:** AI Receptionist call log
**Shows:** 6–8 calls with duration, outcome, attributed patient; one row expanded to show the transcript
**Set up:** Mixed outcomes — booked, enquiry captured, escalated

### `images/features/leads-pipeline.png`
**Screen:** CRM → Leads, board view
**Shows:** All six stage columns populated, owner avatars, at least one overdue flag

### `images/features/consultation-editor.png`
**Screen:** Consultations → in-progress consultation
**Shows:** Structured template fields on the left, annotated diagram on the right
**Set up:** Fill the fields with plausible derma findings. Do not leave placeholder text visible.

### `images/features/annotation-canvas.png`
**Screen:** Annotation canvas, face-front diagram
**Shows:** 4–5 numbered treatment-site markers plus one shaded region
**Set up:** Mark it as a clinician actually would — injectable sites with numbers, not scribble

### `images/features/gallery-grid.png`
**Screen:** Before & After library
**Shows:** Grid filtered by treatment, consent badges visible on each tile
**Set up:** **Use stock or synthetic images only.** Never a real patient, even a consenting one — this page is public and permanent.

### `images/features/gallery-comparison.png`
**Screen:** Photo comparison, slider view
**Shows:** Session 1 versus session 6, dates and session numbers on each side
**Set up:** Same synthetic-image rule

### `images/features/package-detail.png`
**Screen:** Packages → a sold package
**Shows:** Sessions delivered vs remaining, and the financial panel — agreed price, amount received, earned value, unearned advance
**Set up:** 2 of 6 delivered, part-paid, so all four numbers are non-zero and distinct. **This is the shot that proves the accounting works — get it right.**

### `images/features/package-session-allocation.png`
**Screen:** Package → allocate sessions
**Shows:** Six proposed dates across three months at the configured interval

### `images/features/services-catalogue.png`
**Screen:** CRM → Services
**Shows:** Catalogue grouped by category, with price, GST rate, and duration columns
**Set up:** Include a mix of 5% and 18% GST rates — mixed rates are a documented selling point

### `images/features/billing-checkout.png`
**Screen:** Billing → Checkout
**Shows:** 3–4 line items at **different GST rates**, live total with the per-rate tax breakdown expanded
**Set up:** Deliberately mix an 18% service with a 5% product. The breakdown is the whole point.

### `images/features/billing-split-payment.png`
**Screen:** Checkout → payment entry
**Shows:** A single invoice split across UPI and cash, both amounts visible

### `images/features/inventory-list.png`
**Screen:** Inventory
**Shows:** 10–12 products, at least one below reorder level and one nearing expiry, so both alert states are visible

### `images/features/inventory-bom.png`
**Screen:** Service → consumables
**Shows:** A procedure's bill of materials with quantities per session

### `images/features/reports-hub.png`
**Screen:** Reports landing
**Shows:** All report cards, filter controls, export button

### `images/features/reports-schedule.png`
**Screen:** Report → schedule dialog
**Shows:** Cadence, recipient, and WhatsApp delivery option selected

### `images/features/staff-permissions.png`
**Screen:** Staff → Permissions matrix
**Shows:** Full module grid with Doctor and Receptionist columns, at least one non-default toggle

### `images/features/staff-availability.png`
**Screen:** Staff → clinician availability
**Shows:** Working days, hours, breaks, and one leave block

### `images/features/mobile-app.png`
**Screen:** Mobile app — device frame
**Shows:** Two or three screens side by side: calendar, WhatsApp inbox, patient profile
**Set up:** Use a clean device frame. **Capture at 3× on a real device or a high-DPI simulator** — a scaled-up phone screenshot looks cheap next to the desktop shots.

---

## Workflows — 5 images

These tell a story in sequence. Capture them in one session with the same
patient so the narrative holds.

**Story patient: Priya Sharma — 3 of 6 laser sessions remaining, 9 weeks since last visit, package expires in 41 days, ₹18,400 at stake.**

### `images/workflows/winback-01-list.png`
At-Risk list, Priya's row at the top with its reason and value visible

### `images/workflows/winback-02-draft.png`
The AI draft for Priya, grounding context shown

### `images/workflows/winback-03-aisha-books.png`
The WhatsApp thread: message sent → Priya replies → Aisha offers slots → books.
**The most persuasive image on the whole site.** Make the exchange read naturally,
regenerate until it does, and do not fake it by hand — capture a genuine run.

### `images/workflows/package-01-allocation.png`
Six sessions allocated across three months

### `images/workflows/package-02-progress.png`
The same package after 2 of 6 delivered, with earned value and unearned advance visible

---

## Also needed

### `images/og-cover.png` — 1200 × 630
Social share card. Referenced in `docs.json` under `seo.metatags`. Logo, the
line *"RetAI — the clinic OS that books patients back in"*, dark brand background.

### `logo/light.svg` and `logo/dark.svg`
Placeholders are committed. Replace with the real wordmark before publishing.
Light = for light backgrounds (dark ink), dark = for dark backgrounds (cream ink).

### `favicon.svg`
Placeholder committed. Replace with the real mark.

---

## Capture order

Doing it in this order takes about three hours instead of a day, because each
group reuses the state the previous one set up.

1. **Seed the demo tenant** — patients, services, packages, a month of appointments and invoices
2. **Run one genuine WhatsApp conversation** end to end → gives you `winback-03`, `whatsapp-inbox`, `calendar-ai-booking`
3. **Calendar and dashboard** → `hero`, `calendar-day-view`, `quickstart/03`
4. **Patient and clinical** → `patient-profile`, `consultation-editor`, `annotation-canvas`, gallery pair
5. **Packages** → `package-detail`, both allocation shots, `package-02-progress`
6. **Money** → `billing-checkout`, `billing-split-payment`, `services-catalogue`, both inventory shots
7. **Reports** → `reports-hub`, `reports-schedule`, `revenue-recovered-chart`
8. **Admin** → both staff shots, `quickstart/01`, `quickstart/02`
9. **At-risk** → `at-risk-list`, both draft shots, `winback-01`, `winback-02`
10. **Mobile** last, on a device

---

## Final check before commit

- [ ] No real patient name, phone, or photograph anywhere
- [ ] No real staff email or personal phone number
- [ ] No API key, token, or secret visible in any UI or console
- [ ] No browser chrome, extension icons, or OS clock
- [ ] Consistent theme and window size across every image
- [ ] All 35 paths present — `mint dev` shows no broken image
- [ ] Every file under 500 KB

admin/clinic-setup.title: Clinic setup
admin/clinic-setup.description: Branding, GSTIN, invoice numbering, working hours, and automation timing.
admin/clinic-setup.content:
Owner-only. Everything here is set once during [onboarding](#doc-onboarding) and reviewed rarely.

## Clinic profile

| Field | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| Clinic name | Invoices, prescriptions, patient messages |
| Logo | Invoice letterhead, prescription header, photo watermark |
| Address and contact | Invoice footer, what Aisha tells patients who ask for directions |
| GSTIN | Tax invoices |
| Registration numbers | Prescriptions and statutory documents |
| Time zone | Every timestamp in the product |

## Invoice settings


  
Prefix, starting number, and reset behaviour — never, annually, or monthly. Numbers are allocated atomically from a per-clinic sequence: two tills billing at the same instant cannot collide.


> **Warning:** 
Changing the prefix or resetting the sequence mid-year will confuse your accountant and possibly your tax filing. Change it at a financial-year boundary or not at all.


  
  
Payment terms, cancellation policy, and any statutory text your invoices must carry.
  
  
Whether catalogue prices are entered GST-inclusive or exclusive. Set once — changing it later restates how every existing price is interpreted.
  


## Working hours

Clinic opening hours per day, plus holidays and closures. This bounds the calendar and bounds what the AI can offer — Aisha will not book a slot on a day the clinic is shut.

Per-clinician hours are separate and live in [Staff](#doc-features/staff).

## Automation timing

The rules that decide when RetAI messages a patient.

| Automation | Typical setting |
| --- | --- |
| Appointment reminder | 24 hours before, and 2 hours before |
| Confirmation request | On tentative bookings, 48 hours before |
| Post-visit follow-up | 3 days after a completed appointment |
| Aftercare | 1 hour after completion, for services configured to send it |
| Package session due | At the configured session interval |
| Package expiry warning | 30 days before expiry, if sessions remain |
| At-risk re-attempt | 7 days after an unanswered win-back |
| Quiet hours | No automated message before 09:00 or after 20:00 |


> **Tip:** 
  Quiet hours are worth respecting even when a reminder is technically due. A clinic that messages at 11pm gets blocked by patients, and a blocked number cannot reach anyone.



## AI agent settings


  
The agent's name, greeting, and register — formal, warm, or brisk. Set to match how your front desk actually speaks.
  
  
Whether the agent may create appointments or only capture the request for a human. Start restrictive.
  
  
Which topics always go to a human. Clinical questions and complaints are non-removable; you can add more.
  
  
Phrases and claims the agent must never make. Outcome promises and medical claims are enforced by default.
  


## Photo settings

Watermark position and opacity, default masking behaviour, and image retention period. See [Before & After](#doc-features/gallery).

## Related


  

### [Roles & permissions](#doc-admin/roles-and-permissions)
Who sees what.


  

### [Integrations](#doc-admin/integrations/whatsapp)
WhatsApp, calendar, voice, and push.

admin/data-export.title: Data export
admin/data-export.description: Report CSVs, the full clinic archive, per-patient records, and what happens if you leave.
admin/data-export.content:
Your data is yours. There is no export you have to ask permission for and no format that traps you.

## Report exports

Every report in [Reports](#doc-features/reports) has an **Export CSV** button that exports the current filtered view — not a fixed template. Filter first, export second.

## Full clinic export

**Owner only.** Settings → Data export → **Export everything**.

Produces one archive containing:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `patients.csv` | Demographics, contact, flags, lifetime value |
| `appointments.csv` | Every appointment with status, clinician, service |
| `invoices.csv` | Invoice headers with totals and tax |
| `invoice_line_items.csv` | Per-line detail with per-line GST |
| `payments.csv` | Every payment with method and reference |
| `packages.csv` | Sold packages with sessions and financial state |
| `treatments.csv` | Delivered treatments and sessions |
| `consultations.csv` | Consultation records |
| `prescriptions.csv` | Issued prescriptions |
| `messages.csv` | WhatsApp message log with direction and status |
| `calls.csv` | Voice call log with outcomes |
| `inventory.csv` | Products, quantities, and the movement ledger |
| `staff.csv` | Staff records and roles |
| `audit.csv` | The audit trail |

Large exports are prepared in the background; you get a notification and a time-limited download link when ready.


> **Warning:** 
  A full export contains complete patient PHI. Downloading it makes you responsible for how it is stored. Do not email it, do not leave it in a shared drive, and delete it when the purpose it was pulled for is finished. Every export is audited with the staff member's name.



## Photographs

Clinical images export separately because of their size. Choose a date range or a set of patients; you receive a structured archive with a manifest CSV mapping each file to its patient, session, treatment, and consent state.

## Per-patient export

**Patients → open a patient → Actions → Download summary** produces a PDF with demographics, treatment history, prescriptions, packages, and balance.

For a complete machine-readable record of one patient — a DPDP data-portability request — use **Actions → Export full record**, which produces JSON plus that patient's images.


> **Note:** 
  India's DPDP Act gives patients a right of access to their own data. This is the button that satisfies it. See [Data protection](#doc-security/data-protection).



## Accountant handover

For month-end, export from Reports:

1. **GST summary** for the period
2. **Revenue summary**, split by method
3. **Invoice list**, with line items
4. **Refunds and credit notes**
5. **Outstanding ageing** at period end

See [Month-end close](#doc-workflows/month-end-close).

## If you leave RetAI

On termination you may request a complete export at any point during your contract and for **30 days after it ends**. You receive the full clinic archive plus all clinical images.

After that window, your data is deleted per the schedule in [Retention & deletion](#doc-security/retention-and-deletion). We do not hold data hostage and we do not keep it longer than the contract permits.

## API access

Anything exportable through the UI is reachable programmatically. See [Export endpoints](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/export).

admin/data-import.title: Data import
admin/data-import.description: Bringing your existing patients, services, packages, and stock into RetAI.
admin/data-import.content:
Migration is run by the RetAI team during [onboarding](#doc-onboarding). This page tells you what to send and what happens to it.


> **Note:** 
  Send whatever format you already have — a CSV export, an Excel workbook, even photographs of a printed price list. We normalise it. The fields below are what we extract, not a format you must produce.



## Patients

**Required**

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Name | |
| Phone | Any format. We normalise to E.164 (`+919876543210`). |

**Strongly recommended**

| Field | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Last visit date | Without it, at-risk scoring has no baseline and stays quiet for weeks |
| Treatment history | Drives at-risk cadence and gives Aisha context in conversation |
| Package/session state | Unredeemed sessions are your fastest recoverable revenue |
| Email, DOB, gender, address | Reporting and demographics |
| Referral source | Lead-source reporting |
| Allergies and clinical flags | Safety. Send these even if you send nothing else optional. |
| Outstanding balance | So the front desk sees it on day one |


> **Warning:** 
  **Phone numbers are the identity key.** A number stored without a country code will not match an inbound WhatsApp message, and that patient will appear to RetAI as a stranger. Our importer fixes what it can and reports what it cannot — review that report.



## Services

Name, category, price, GST rate, duration, and the clinicians who deliver it. Add the patient-facing description if you have one; if not, we draft them and you approve — this is what Aisha reads to patients.

## Packages

Name, component services with session counts, list price, validity period, and session interval.

**In-flight packages** — courses your patients have already partly used — need sessions total, sessions already delivered, agreed price, and amount received. Without those four numbers, revenue recognition starts wrong and stays wrong.

## Inventory

Product name, SKU, unit, current quantity, purchase price, selling price, GST rate, reorder level, and batch/expiry where applicable. Vendors optional at go-live.

## Staff

Name, work email, phone, role, and — for clinicians — registration number, specialty, and which services they deliver.

## What happens to your file


  
We check for missing required fields, malformed phone numbers, impossible dates, and duplicate records. You get a report before anything is written.
  
  
Phone numbers to E.164, dates to a single format, currency strings to numbers, names to consistent casing.
  
  
Candidate duplicates are matched on phone first, then name plus date of birth. Ambiguous cases go on a review list rather than being merged silently.
  
  
Imported into your demo tenant first. Your team checks a sample against the source before anything reaches the live tenant.
  
  
Written to your live tenant, with an import reference on every record so the batch is reversible.
  


## After import

- Check ten patients at random against your old system
- Confirm package session counts on your five most valuable in-flight packages
- Confirm at-risk begins populating — it needs last-visit dates to have imported
- Test one WhatsApp message from an imported patient's number and confirm it attaches to the right record


> **Tip:** 
  The WhatsApp test is the one people skip and the one that catches phone-normalisation problems. Do it before go-live, not after.



## Ongoing import

Beyond migration, you can bulk-add via CSV in **Patients → Import** and **Services → Import**, or push records from a website form through the [API](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/crm).

## Related


  

### [Onboarding plan](#doc-onboarding)
Where import sits in the rollout.


  

### [Data export](#doc-admin/data-export)
Getting your data back out.

admin/integrations/google-calendar.title: Connect Google Calendar
admin/integrations/google-calendar.description: Two-way sync between RetAI appointments and your clinicians' Google Calendars.
admin/integrations/google-calendar.content:
Clinicians already live in Google Calendar. Rather than asking them to stop, RetAI syncs both ways.

## What sync does


  

### Push
An appointment created in RetAI — by staff or by Aisha — appears on the clinician's Google Calendar within seconds, with patient name, service, and duration.


  

### Pull
Personal events the clinician blocks in Google appear in RetAI as busy time. Neither staff nor the AI will book over their lunch or their child's school run.




## Connecting


  
  
You are redirected to Google to grant calendar access.
  
  
Connect the account whose calendar should sync — not a shared clinic account, unless that genuinely is the clinician's working calendar.
  
  
RetAI requests calendar read and write. It requests nothing else — no Gmail, no Drive, no contacts.
  
  
Pick which calendar receives clinic appointments. A dedicated "Clinic" calendar is cleaner than the personal default.
  
  
Create a test appointment in RetAI and confirm it appears in Google. Then block an hour in Google and confirm RetAI shows it as busy.
  



> **Note:** 
  Each clinician connects their own calendar. There is no way for one staff member to connect a colleague's calendar on their behalf — the consent must come from the account holder.



## What is stored

RetAI stores a Google refresh token so sync can continue without re-authorising daily. That token is **encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM** under a key held separately from the application session secret.

Revoking access in your Google account permissions ends the connection immediately; the stored token becomes useless.

## Sync behaviour

| Action in RetAI | Effect in Google |
| --- | --- |
| Appointment created | Event created |
| Appointment moved | Event moved |
| Appointment cancelled | Event deleted |
| Status changed | Event title updated |

| Action in Google | Effect in RetAI |
| --- | --- |
| Event created on the synced calendar | Shown as busy; that time cannot be booked |
| Event moved | Busy time moves |
| Event deleted | Busy time cleared |


> **Warning:** 
  Editing a RetAI-created event *inside Google* is not a supported way to reschedule. The clinical record, the reminder, and the patient's expectation all live in RetAI. Reschedule there; Google follows.



## Privacy of event detail

Choose what appears in the Google event title:

| Setting | Google shows |
| --- | --- |
| Full detail | Patient name and service |
| Service only | Service name, no patient name |
| Busy only | "Clinic appointment" |


> **Tip:** 
  If a clinician's Google Calendar is shared with anyone outside the clinic — a spouse, an assistant, a public availability link — use **Service only** or **Busy only**. A shared calendar is a disclosure path, and patient names on it are a data-protection problem.



## Disconnecting

Settings → Integrations → Google Calendar → **Disconnect**. The stored token is deleted. Events already pushed remain in Google; delete them there if you want them gone.

## Troubleshooting


  
Usually the Google account changed its password or revoked access. Reconnect.
  
  
Confirm the events are on the *selected* calendar. Events on a different calendar in the same account are not read.
  
  
Usually two connections to the same calendar from different staff accounts. Disconnect one.

admin/integrations/push-notifications.title: Push notifications
admin/integrations/push-notifications.description: Mobile alerts for inbound patient messages, escalations, and overdue follow-ups.
admin/integrations/push-notifications.content:
Push notifications are how a clinic owner finds out a patient messaged at 9pm without watching the inbox.

## Enabling


  
iOS or Android. See [Mobile app](#doc-features/mobile).
  
  
Same account as the web.
  
  
If you dismissed the prompt, enable it in your device's system settings for the RetAI app. The app cannot re-prompt once dismissed.
  
  
Settings → Notifications, per device. Two phones can have different settings for the same account.
  


## Available notifications

| Notification | Default | Recommended for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inbound patient WhatsApp message | On | Front desk, owner |
| Thread escalated by the AI | On | Whoever handles escalations |
| Appointment booked by the AI | Off | Owner, during the first fortnight |
| Appointment cancelled by a patient | On | Front desk |
| Overdue lead follow-up assigned to you | On | Anyone who owns leads |
| Low stock alert | Off | Owner, practice manager |
| Day-end report ready | Off | Owner |

## Content-free by design


> **Note:** 
  Push payloads never contain patient names or message content. The notification tells you *that* a message arrived; tapping it opens the app, which then loads the data under your authenticated session.



That means a notification sitting on a lock screen in a waiting room discloses nothing. It also means you cannot read a message from the notification shade — you have to open the app. That trade is deliberate.

## Device management

Each device that signs in registers itself for push. Signing out deregisters it.


> **Warning:** 
  Sold or lost phone? Sign out on it if you can. If you cannot, have an owner deactivate and reactivate your staff account — that invalidates the session and stops delivery to that device.



## Troubleshooting


  
Check system notification permission for the RetAI app, then check per-notification toggles in Settings → Notifications, then sign out and back in to re-register the device.
  
  
Usually battery optimisation on Android suspending background delivery. Exclude RetAI from battery optimisation.
  
  
An old device still holds a registration. Sign out on it, or have an owner cycle your account.
  
  
The same account signed in on two devices with the same alerts enabled. Turn the alert off on one.

admin/integrations/voice.title: Voice setup
admin/integrations/voice.description: Numbers, call routing, agent configuration, and recording policy for the AI Receptionist.
admin/integrations/voice.content:
> **Note:** 
  Voice is a separate plan tier. If it is not enabled for your clinic the module is hidden and no calls are answered — nothing else changes.



## What you need

- A phone number for the AI to answer on. Either a new number, or your existing clinic line with conditional forwarding to it.
- An escalation number where live transfers go.
- Your call-recording consent wording, matching what your jurisdiction requires.

## Answer policy


  

### Overflow only
The AI answers only after the clinic line rings unanswered past a threshold. **Start here.**


  

### After hours only
The AI answers outside working hours. Humans take everything during opening.


  

### All calls
The AI answers first, always, transferring to a human when needed.





> **Tip:** 
  Overflow-only with **enquiry capture, no booking** is the right first fortnight. Read the transcripts, fix the treatment descriptions that produced awkward answers, then widen. Clinics that switch everything on at once end up distrusting transcripts they never read.



## Agent configuration

| Setting | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Greeting | The first line the caller hears. Include the clinic name. |
| Voice | Several options including Indian English |
| Languages | Additional languages the agent will switch to on hearing them |
| Booking permission | May the agent create appointments, or only capture the request? |
| Escalation number | Where live transfers land |
| Escalation triggers | Clinical questions and complaints are non-removable; add your own |
| Maximum call duration | A safety ceiling |
| Recording retention | How long audio is kept before automatic deletion |

## What the agent may say

It reads from your [service catalogue](#doc-features/services) — treatment descriptions, prices, and durations. It reads the patient's record when the caller's number matches one.

It is forbidden from promising outcomes, making medical claims, inventing prices or offers, and confirming an appointment that was not actually created.


> **Warning:** 
  The patient-facing description on each service is what a caller hears. Write those fields as you would want them spoken aloud to a stranger. The agent will not invent claims — but it will faithfully repeat one you wrote.



## Recording and consent

RetAI plays a configurable consent announcement at the start of every recorded call.


> **Warning:** 
  The wording is your clinic's legal responsibility, not ours. It must match what your jurisdiction requires for recording a call. Have it reviewed before you go live. See [Data protection](#doc-security/data-protection).



Recordings are encrypted at rest, scoped to your clinic, and deleted automatically at your configured retention period.

## Outbound calls

Triggered from a patient record — appointment confirmation, package-expiry reminder, or a win-back for a lapsed high-value patient. Outbound calling is rate-limited per clinic to prevent a misconfiguration from calling your entire patient list.

## Attribution and safety

A call's clinic and patient are resolved **from the phone number, on the server** — never from the call payload. A spoofed or malformed payload cannot attribute a call to the wrong clinic. Call events are deduplicated at the database level, so a retried webhook cannot create a duplicate call record.

## Reviewing calls

The call log shows caller, duration, outcome, and attributed patient. Open a call for the transcript, the recording, and any appointment or lead it created.


> **Tip:** 
  Read ten transcripts a month, permanently. It is the cheapest quality control in the product, and it usually surfaces a service description that needs rewording rather than an AI failure.



## Turning it off

Settings → Integrations → Voice → **Disable**. Calls stop being answered immediately. Existing call records, transcripts, and recordings are retained per your retention setting.

admin/integrations/whatsapp.title: Connect WhatsApp
admin/integrations/whatsapp.description: Connect your WhatsApp Business number so patients can message the clinic and Aisha can reply.
admin/integrations/whatsapp.content:
This is the integration that turns RetAI from a records system into a retention engine. It is set up by the RetAI team during [onboarding](#doc-onboarding); this page explains what happens and what you need to have ready.

## What you need


  

### A phone number
Either a new number or your existing clinic number — provided it is **not currently registered on the WhatsApp consumer or Business app**. A number can only live in one place.


  

### Business verification details
Registered clinic name, address, website, and business category. These are what appear as your verified display name.





> **Warning:** 
  If your clinic number is currently in use on the WhatsApp Business *app* on someone's phone, migrating it to the API means that app stops working for that number. Decide this before you start — reversing it is slow. Most clinics take a fresh number and forward the old one.



## Setup


  
Registered against your clinic's tenant.
  
  
Submitted with your details. Verification typically takes 1–3 business days and is what gets your clinic name shown to patients instead of a bare number.
  
  
Inbound messages are routed to your clinic. Every inbound request is signature-verified — a forged webhook is rejected before it reaches any data.
  
  
Reminders, confirmations, and follow-ups are submitted for approval. Approval usually takes hours.
  
  
Aisha's persona, tone, escalation rules, and forbidden claims are set from your [clinic settings](#doc-admin/clinic-setup).
  
  
We verify, with you watching:

- A message from a known patient's number attaches to the right record
- A message from an unknown number creates a patient
- Aisha answers a treatment question correctly from your catalogue
- Aisha books an appointment into a genuinely free slot
- A reminder sends at the configured time
- An invoice delivers as a PDF link
  


## Templates versus conversation

WhatsApp distinguishes two message types, and the distinction shapes what RetAI can do when.

| Type | When usable | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Template** | Any time, pre-approved wording | Reminders, confirmations, follow-ups, win-backs |
| **Session** | Within 24 hours of the patient's last message | Free-form conversation, including everything Aisha says |


> **Tip:** 
  This is why a patient reply matters so much. Once they message you, a 24-hour window opens in which the conversation can be completely natural. Aisha is designed to get useful work done inside that window rather than pushing more templates at them.



## Reliability properties worth knowing

- **Inbound messages are deduplicated at the database level.** WhatsApp retries webhooks on any hiccup; a retry cannot produce a second reply from Aisha.
- **Outbound messages cannot double-send.** Queued messages are claimed atomically before delivery.
- **Inbound is rate-limited per phone number.** A malfunctioning or malicious sender cannot exhaust your AI quota.
- **Unattributable messages are dropped, not guessed.** If a message cannot be resolved to a clinic with certainty, nothing is written and no reply is sent. Silence beats replying into the wrong clinic's context.

## Number reputation

WhatsApp scores business numbers on how patients react to them. A number that gets blocked or reported drops in quality and eventually loses sending capacity.

RetAI protects yours by:

- Rate-limiting and spreading bulk sends over time
- Respecting quiet hours on automated messages
- Not re-sending an unanswered message more than the configured attempts
- Honouring opt-outs permanently


> **Warning:** 
  The fastest way to damage a number is a large blast of near-identical promotional messages. Use the [at-risk list](#doc-features/at-risk), which personalises per patient, rather than treating RetAI as a broadcast tool.



## Opt-outs

A patient who asks to stop receiving messages is opted out permanently and immediately. They can still be replied to if *they* message you; they will receive no automated message again unless they explicitly opt back in.

## Troubleshooting


  
A phone-format mismatch. The patient record likely holds a number without a country code. Fix the record; history reattaches.
  
  
Check that the thread has not been taken over by a staff member — a taken-over thread is deliberately silent from the AI. Then check the agent is enabled in clinic settings.
  
  
Check template approval status, and check the reminder is not falling inside quiet hours.
  
  
Business verification is incomplete or the display name is pending review. This is on WhatsApp's side; we chase it.
  


More in [Troubleshooting](#doc-help/troubleshooting).

admin/roles-and-permissions.title: Roles & permissions
admin/roles-and-permissions.description: The three roles, the module matrix, and how access is actually enforced.
admin/roles-and-permissions.content:
## The three roles


  

### Owner
Every module, always. Cannot be restricted — a clinic must not be able to lock out its own administrator.


  

### Doctor
Clinical and commercial modules. Configurable.


  

### Receptionist
Front-of-house modules. Configurable.




## The module matrix

**Staff → Permissions.** Toggle any module for Doctor or Receptionist. Changes apply on the staff member's next page load.

| Module | Doctor default | Receptionist default |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Overview | ✅ always | ✅ always |
| AI Calendar | ✅ | ✅ |
| All Patients | ✅ | ✅ |
| WhatsApp Inbox | ✅ | ✅ |
| AI Receptionist | ✅ | ✅ |
| Leads Pipeline | ✅ | ✅ |
| Services | ✅ | ✅ |
| Before & After | ✅ | ✅ |
| Treatment Packages | ✅ | ✅ |
| At-Risk Patients | ✅ | ❌ |
| Consultations & Rx | ✅ | ❌ |
| Billing | ✅ | ❌ |
| Inventory | ✅ | ❌ |
| Staff | ❌ | ❌ |

Two defaults are deliberate:

- **Reception gets photos and packages.** They capture the images and they sell the courses. Locking them out creates a bottleneck at the doctor.
- **Reception does not get prescriptions.** Prescribing is clinical. Grant it if your practice works differently, but it is off until an owner decides.


> **Note:** 
  **Overview can never be revoked.** Every signed-in staff member sees the overview screen. There is no configuration that produces a user who can log in and see nothing.



## How enforcement actually works

This matters more than the toggles.


  
No valid session → API calls return 401, page requests redirect to sign-in.
  
  
The session must correspond to a current staff record. A staff record that has been deactivated fails here, even if the session was issued before deactivation.
  
  
Every module page checks access **on the server as its first action**. Navigating directly to a module URL you lack access to returns nothing — the gating is not hidden in the browser.
  
  
Every query is scoped to your clinic before it runs. Clinic identity comes from your session, never from a URL parameter or request body — so editing an ID in a request cannot reach another clinic's data.
  



> **Warning:** 
  A deactivated staff member loses access within minutes, not at session expiry. Role and clinic are re-read from the staff record periodically, so de-provisioning takes effect quickly and **fails closed** — a missing staff record grants nothing rather than defaulting to something.



## Multi-location groups

A group owner can hold access across locations and switch between them. Every other role is bound to a single clinic. There is no view anywhere that shows two clinics' patients side by side.

## What is always audited

Regardless of role:

- Sign-ins and sign-in failures
- Permission changes
- Discounts granted, refunds, and invoice cancellations
- Patient record edits
- Data exports
- Photo exports and collection additions

See [Access control](#doc-security/access-control).

## Recommended starting configuration


  
Owner and doctor are the same person. One receptionist on defaults. Nothing to change.
  
  
Doctors on defaults but with **Billing off** unless they take payment themselves. A practice manager on the Receptionist role with Billing and Inventory granted.
  
  
Counsellor on the Receptionist role with Billing granted (they build quotations) and Inventory off.

api-reference/authentication.title: Authentication
api-reference/authentication.description: How API requests are authenticated and scoped.
api-reference/authentication.content:
## Session authentication

The API authenticates with the same signed session cookie the web application uses. Requests from a signed-in browser session are authenticated automatically.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mechanism | Signed JWT session cookie |
| Idle lifetime | 8 hours |
| Refresh | On activity |
| Unauthenticated API request | `401` JSON |
| Unauthenticated page request | `307` redirect to sign-in |

## What a valid session means

Authentication is not a single check at issue time. On each request:

1. The session signature is verified
2. The session must correspond to a **currently active** staff record
3. Role and clinic are re-read from that staff record periodically, not trusted from the token for its full lifetime


> **Warning:** 
  A deactivated staff member's session stops working within minutes, even though the token has not expired. A missing staff record grants nothing — the failure mode is closed, not open.



## Authorisation

Two further checks after authentication:


  
Endpoints belonging to a module require that module to be permitted for your role. See [Roles & permissions](#doc-admin/roles-and-permissions).
  
  
Every query is scoped to the clinic derived from your session. Clinic identity is **never** read from a parameter, body, or payload.
  


## Self-authenticating endpoints

Six endpoints are reachable without a session because they are called by external systems. Each authenticates itself:

| Endpoint | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/whatsapp` | Cryptographic signature over URL and sorted parameters |
| `GET /api/whatsapp` | Provider webhook verification token |
| `POST /api/bolna/webhook` | Shared secret via header or query; **fails closed in production** when unconfigured |
| `GET /api/cron/followups` | Secret header, compared in constant time |
| `GET /api/cron/google-calendar-sync` | Secret header, compared in constant time |
| `GET /api/integrations/google/callback` | HMAC-signed, 10-minute-lifetime authorisation state |


> **Warning:** 
  These are matched **exactly**, never by prefix. `/api/whatsapp` is public; `/api/whatsapp/send` and `/api/whatsapp/inbox` are session-protected. A prefix rule here would expose both — which is exactly the kind of mistake this design exists to prevent.



## Machine-to-machine access

There is no issued API key today. If you need server-to-server integration, contact us rather than automating a browser session — we will discuss a proper mechanism.

## Related


  

### [Errors](#doc-api-reference/errors)
Status codes and error shapes.


  

### [Rate limits](#doc-api-reference/rate-limits)
Which endpoints are limited, and how.

Any valid status.

ISO 8601. Reschedules; `ends_at` recomputes from the service duration unless supplied.

Updating an appointment is not an inert write:

| Change | Triggers |
| --- | --- |
| `status` → `completed` | Post-visit follow-up queued; aftercare sent if configured; package session incremented; consumables deducted |
| `status` → `cancelled` | Pending reminders cancelled; Google Calendar event removed; slot freed |
| `starts_at` changed | Reminders re-queued; Google Calendar event moved |
| `clinician_id` changed | Google Calendar event moves between calendars |

`GET /api/export/clinic`

Full clinic dataset as a multi-file archive.

ISO 8601 date. Omit for everything.

ISO 8601 date.


  Comma-separated: `patients`, `appointments`, `invoices`, `payments`, `packages`, `treatments`, `consultations`, `prescriptions`, `messages`, `calls`, `inventory`, `staff`, `audit`. Omit for all.

> **Warning:** 
  A full export is complete patient PHI in a file. Once you have downloaded it, its security is entirely yours. Do not email it, do not put it on a shared drive, and delete it when the purpose it was pulled for is done.



## Billing export

`GET /api/billing/export`

CSV of invoices and line items — the accountant-facing export.

ISO 8601 date.

ISO 8601 date.

`csv` or `json`.


Columns include invoice number, issue date, patient reference, line description, quantity, unit price, discount, **per-line GST rate and tax amount**, line total, payment method, and payment reference.


> **Warning:** 
  Reconcile tax from `tax_amount` per line. Do not apply a single rate to the invoice subtotal — mixed-rate invoices will not balance.

Available in the UI at **Patients → Actions → Export full record**, producing JSON plus that patient's images. This is the DPDP data-portability path. See [Data export](#doc-admin/data-export).

Exports are heavy. Limit yourself to one full clinic export at a time; concurrent large exports will be queued rather than run in parallel.


> **Tip:** 
  For recurring reporting, export incrementally with `from` and `to` rather than pulling everything each run. Faster for you and gentler on the database.

## Place an outbound call

`POST /api/voice/call`


`confirmation`, `win_back`, `package_expiry`, `follow_up`.

> **Warning:** 
  **This rings a real phone.** Rate limited to 10 per minute per clinic — protection against a runaway loop dialling your entire patient list, not a licence to sit at the limit. Never blind-retry.

A call's clinic and patient are resolved **from the phone number, on the server**, never from the provider payload. A spoofed or malformed payload cannot attribute a call to the wrong clinic.

Call records are deduplicated on the provider's call ID at the database level, so a retried event cannot create a duplicate.

## Send

`POST /api/whatsapp/send`

Either this or `phone`.

E.164. Used when messaging a non-patient.

Message text.

Approved template name. Required outside the 24-hour session window.

Placeholder values for the template.
