api-reference/errors.title: Errors
api-reference/errors.description: Status codes, error shapes, and how to handle each.
api-reference/errors.content:
## Error shape

```json
{
  "error": "Human-readable message",
  "code": "MACHINE_READABLE_CODE"
}
```

## Status codes

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | Success | |
| `201` | Created | |
| `400` | Malformed request, or clinic scope could not be resolved | Fix the request. Do not retry unchanged. |
| `401` | No valid session | Re-authenticate. Do not retry the same request. |
| `403` | Authenticated, but your role lacks access to this module | Ask an owner to grant it. Retrying will not help. |
| `404` | Not found, **or not in your clinic** | See the note below. |
| `409` | Conflict — for example a duplicate on a unique constraint | Usually means the operation already succeeded. Check before retrying. |
| `429` | Rate limited | Back off and retry. See [Rate limits](#doc-api-reference/rate-limits). |
| `500` | Server error | Retry with backoff. Report if it persists. |


> **Warning:** 
  **`404` does not distinguish "does not exist" from "belongs to another clinic."** This is deliberate — a distinguishable response would confirm the existence of records in other tenants, which is an information leak. Do not build logic that infers existence from a 404.



## Common error codes

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid session |
| `FORBIDDEN_MODULE` | Role lacks access to this module |
| `CLINIC_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED` | Clinic could not be derived from the session. Almost always a staff record problem. |
| `INVALID_PHONE` | Phone number not resolvable to E.164 |
| `INVALID_DATE` | Date or time could not be parsed |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | See the retry guidance |
| `DUPLICATE` | Unique constraint hit — the record likely already exists |
| `VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE` | A downstream provider failed. Check [status](https://status.retai.tech). |

## Retry guidance


  
Message sends and invoice creation have real-world side effects. On an ambiguous failure, **check whether it succeeded before retrying.** A duplicate WhatsApp message to a patient is worse than a delayed one, and a duplicate invoice is a tax problem.
  
  
Start at one second, double each attempt, cap at five attempts.
  
  
Nothing about the request will change on its own.
  
  
A conflict on a unique constraint usually means your first attempt landed. Verify rather than retrying.
  


## Webhook error semantics

If you operate a webhook consumer, note that RetAI's own inbound webhooks deliberately return `500` on an unexpected failure so the provider retries, and treat a duplicate-key error as success so a retry does not create a duplicate record. That combination — retry on real failure, idempotent on redelivery — is the pattern to copy.

api-reference/introduction.title: API introduction
api-reference/introduction.description: Base URL, conventions, and what the RetAI API is for.
api-reference/introduction.content:
The RetAI API is used for integrations — pushing website enquiries into the leads pipeline, pulling reporting data into a warehouse, or syncing with practice software you already run.


> **Note:** 
  The API is session-authenticated and scoped to the signed-in staff member's clinic. It is not currently a public partner API with issued keys. If you need machine-to-machine access, talk to us — we will not tell you to script a browser session.



## Base URL

```
https://www.retai.tech/api
```

## Conventions

| Aspect | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Format | JSON request and response bodies |
| Methods | `GET` read, `POST` create, `PATCH` update, `DELETE` remove |
| Timestamps | ISO 8601 with timezone |
| Money | Numbers in rupees, two decimal places |
| Phone numbers | E.164 (`+919876543210`) on the way in and out |
| IDs | UUIDs |

## Clinic scope


> **Warning:** 
  **Every endpoint is scoped to the clinic of the authenticated session.** There is no `clinic_id` parameter you can pass, because clinic identity is never read from user input. This is a security property, not a missing feature: it is what makes it impossible to reach another clinic's data by editing a request.



## Endpoint groups


  

### [Patients](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/patients)
Read and search patient records.


  

### [Appointments](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/appointments)
List and update appointments.


  

### [Billing](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/billing)
Services, invoices, checkout, PDFs, and delivery.


  

### [WhatsApp](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/whatsapp)
Inbox and outbound send.


  

### [Voice](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/voice)
Call log and outbound calls.


  

### [CRM](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/crm)
Leads, status, and presence.


  

### [Export](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/export)
Clinic and billing exports.


  

### [Webhooks](#doc-api-reference/webhooks/whatsapp-inbound)
Inbound message, voice event, and scheduled-job endpoints.




## Before you build


  
Several endpoints are rate-limited, and the limits are per-instance rather than globally coordinated. See [Rate limits](#doc-api-reference/rate-limits).
  
  
Sessions expire after 8 hours idle. A `401` means sign in again, not retry the same request.
  
  
Invoice writes are sequential rather than a single transaction. Verify a created invoice before acting on it as complete.
  
  
We would rather know an integration exists than discover it in a traffic spike. It also means we tell you before a breaking change instead of after.

api-reference/rate-limits.title: Rate limits
api-reference/rate-limits.description: Which endpoints are limited, at what rate, and how the limits actually behave.
api-reference/rate-limits.content:
## Limits

| Endpoint | Limit | Window key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/ai/generate-reminder` | 20 / minute | Clinic |
| `POST /api/whatsapp/send` | 30 / minute | Clinic |
| `POST /api/voice/call` | 10 / minute | Clinic |
| `POST /api/whatsapp` (inbound) | 15 / minute | Per sending phone number |
| Credential sign-in | 10 per 5 minutes | Per IP address |

## Why these five

Each protects something specific:


  

### AI generation
Cost. A runaway loop calling a language model is expensive fast.


  

### WhatsApp send
Your number's reputation. A burst of near-identical messages is how a business number gets restricted.


  

### Voice calls
Real money and real phones ringing. A misconfiguration should not dial your whole patient list.


  

### Inbound per phone
A malfunctioning or hostile sender should not be able to exhaust your AI quota.




Sign-in limiting is per IP, against credential stuffing.

## How the limit actually behaves


> **Warning:** 
  Rate limiting is a **fixed window, per running application instance** — it is not globally coordinated across instances. The effective ceiling is the stated limit multiplied by the number of instances currently serving traffic.

  It is abuse and runaway-loop protection. It is **not** a hard billing cap, and you should not design an integration that relies on it to bound your costs.



Being a fixed window rather than a sliding one also means a burst can straddle a window boundary and briefly exceed the nominal rate. Both properties are stated because a vague claim here would mislead someone building against it.

## When you hit a limit

You receive `429` with:

```json
{
  "error": "Rate limit exceeded",
  "code": "RATE_LIMITED"
}
```

Back off exponentially — start at one second, double each attempt, cap at five attempts.

## Designing to stay under


  
RetAI's own bulk campaigns spread over time deliberately. If you are sending programmatically, do the same — both for the limit and for your number's reputation.
  
  
List endpoints accept filters. One filtered request beats two hundred single-record requests.
  
  
The service catalogue changes rarely. Do not fetch it per message.
  
  
On an ambiguous failure, check whether it delivered before retrying. Duplicate messages to patients are worse than delayed ones.
  


## Higher limits

If a legitimate integration needs more headroom, talk to us. We would rather raise a limit than have you work around it.

api-reference/webhooks/cron.title: Scheduled jobs
api-reference/webhooks/cron.description: The background workers that drain the follow-up queue and sync calendars.
api-reference/webhooks/cron.content:
Two scheduled endpoints, each authenticated by a secret header compared in **constant time**.


> **Note:** 
  These are documented because their behaviour explains guarantees you rely on elsewhere — particularly why a patient never receives the same message twice.



## Follow-up queue drain

`GET /api/cron/followups`

Runs every few minutes. Sends reminders, follow-ups, aftercare, and package-expiry messages that have come due.


  
Pending items with a trigger time in the past. Deliberately **across clinics** — one worker serves everyone.
  
  
Each item is claimed with a conditional update. **This is what makes overlapping runs safe** — two workers cannot both claim the same item, so a patient cannot be messaged twice.
  
  
With a delivery latch, so a bookkeeping retry can never re-send to the patient.
  
  
  



> **Warning:** 
  **Delivered-but-unlogged items are deliberately parked, never re-claimed.** They are flagged for manual reconciliation instead.

  The reasoning is explicit: a duplicate message to a patient is worse than a missing log row. Given an ambiguous state, RetAI chooses the missing log row every time.



## Google Calendar pull sync

`GET /api/cron/google-calendar-sync`

Runs periodically. Pulls changes from every connected Google Calendar so externally-created events appear as busy time in RetAI.

Iterates all connections across clinics by design — one worker, all tenants, each write still scoped to the clinic that owns the connection.

Stored refresh tokens are decrypted per connection (AES-256-GCM) and used only for that connection's calendar.

## Authentication

Both require a secret header, compared in constant time.


> **Warning:** 
  Constant-time comparison is not incidental. A naive string comparison leaks timing information that can be used to recover the secret byte by byte. Any endpoint of yours that compares a secret should do the same.



## Failure behaviour

| Situation | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Missing or wrong secret | `403`, nothing runs |
| One item fails | Logged and skipped; the run continues |
| Whole run fails | `500`; the next scheduled run picks up where it stopped |
| Overlapping runs | Safe by design — atomic claiming prevents double-processing |

## What this means for you


  
A reminder due at 15:00 sends within a few minutes of 15:00, not at exactly 15:00.
  
  
Items stay pending until claimed. A skipped run means slightly late messages, not lost ones.
  
  
An item that comes due inside quiet hours waits rather than sending.

api-reference/webhooks/voice-events.title: Voice events
api-reference/webhooks/voice-events.description: The public webhook that receives call outcomes from the voice provider.
api-reference/webhooks/voice-events.content:
`POST /api/bolna/webhook`

Public by necessity, authenticated by a shared secret supplied as a header or query parameter.


> **Warning:** 
  **This endpoint fails closed in production.** If the shared secret is not configured, it rejects every request rather than accepting unauthenticated ones. A misconfiguration produces silence, not an open door.



## Processing


  
Rejected outright if invalid or unconfigured in production.
  
  
In-progress events are acknowledged and ignored. Only completed calls create records.
  
  
A pre-check for efficiency, with a database uniqueness constraint as the authority.
  
  

> **Warning:** 
The clinic is read from the **patient record**, never from the payload. A spoofed or malformed payload cannot attribute a call to the wrong clinic.


  
  
With transcript, outcome, duration, and any appointment or lead it created.
  


## Response semantics

| Situation | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Processed | `200` |
| Duplicate call ID | `200` — the unique-constraint violation is treated as success, so a retry cannot create a duplicate |
| Invalid or missing secret | `403` |
| In-progress event | `200`, ignored |
| Unexpected failure | `500`, so the provider retries |


> **Note:** 
  Returning `500` on unexpected failure is deliberate. A dropped call record is worse than a retried one, and the deduplication constraint makes retries safe.



## Payload

Provider-defined. RetAI reads: call identifier, phone number, direction, start time, duration, status, transcript, and any structured outcome the agent produced.


> **Warning:** 
  RetAI does **not** read clinic or patient identity from the payload, even when present. That resolution happens server-side from the phone number. If you are debugging attribution, look at the phone number and the patient record — not at what the payload claims.



## Related


  

### [Voice endpoints](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/voice)
Reading the call log and placing outbound calls.


  

### [Voice setup](#doc-admin/integrations/voice)
Configuration and routing.

api-reference/webhooks/whatsapp-inbound.title: WhatsApp inbound
api-reference/webhooks/whatsapp-inbound.description: The public webhook that receives patient messages, and everything that happens after.
api-reference/webhooks/whatsapp-inbound.content:
> **Warning:** 
  This endpoint is **public by necessity** — the provider must be able to reach it without a session. It authenticates every request cryptographically instead.

  It is matched **exactly**, never by prefix. `/api/whatsapp` is public; `/api/whatsapp/send` and `/api/whatsapp/inbox` require a session. A prefix rule here would expose both.



## Verification

`GET /api/whatsapp` — provider webhook verification handshake, using a verification token.

## Receiving a message

`POST /api/whatsapp`

Authenticated by a cryptographic signature over the request URL and its sorted parameters. **An unsigned or incorrectly signed request is rejected before it reaches any data.**

## What happens on a valid message

```mermaid
flowchart TD
A[Provider POST] --> B[Verify signature]
B -->|invalid| Z[Reject]
B -->|valid| C[Deduplicate on provider message ID]
C -->|already seen| Y[Return OK, do nothing]
C -->|new| D[Normalise phone to E.164]
D --> E[Rate limit per phone]
E --> F{Resolve clinic + patientserver-side}
F -->|unattributable| X[Drop: nothing written, no reply]
F -->|resolved| G[Log inbound message]
G --> H[Push notification, content-free]
H --> I[AI: history + treatment plan + catalogue]
I --> J{Reply or tool?}
J -->|reply| K[Claims filter]
J -->|tool| L[Execute with server-resolved clinic + patient]
L --> M[e.g. create appointment]
K --> N[Send and log outbound]
M --> N
```

## The properties that matter


  
A uniqueness constraint on the provider's message ID is the authority. Providers retry webhooks on any hiccup; a retried delivery **cannot** produce a second AI reply.
  

  
If a message cannot be resolved to a clinic with certainty, **nothing is written and no reply is sent.** Silence beats replying into the wrong clinic's context.
  

  
Clinic and patient are resolved from the verified sender *before* the model is called, and are passed to any tool execution from that server-side resolution — never from model output.

Precisely: a prompt injection can choose **which tool runs**. It cannot choose **whose record it runs against**.
  

  
The notification carries a device token and a generic string. Patient name and message content are never in the payload — which is why a notification on a lock screen discloses nothing.
  

  
15 per minute per sender. A malfunctioning or hostile sender cannot exhaust a clinic's AI quota.
  


## AI tool execution

When the model decides to act rather than reply, the tool runs with server-resolved identity. For `book_appointment`:


  
  

##### Find clinicians qualified for the service

From the service catalogue. No mapped clinician means no booking — the request escalates instead.
  
  

##### Create the appointment

The commit point. Everything after is bookkeeping.
  
  

##### Bookkeeping, each independently fault-tolerant

Google Calendar push, reminder queueing, follow-up scheduling. A failure in any one of these does **not** roll back the appointment — a booked patient with a missing calendar entry is far better than a patient told they are booked when they are not.
  


## Hallucinated-confirmation interception

A reply claiming an appointment that no tool actually created is intercepted before it reaches the patient.


> **Note:** 
  This is the guardrail that matters most in practice. A model that occasionally says "you're booked for Thursday" without booking anything is worse than no automation at all — so that specific failure is checked for explicitly rather than trusted not to happen.



## Response semantics

| Situation | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Processed | `200` |
| Duplicate delivery | `200` — treated as success so the provider stops retrying |
| Invalid signature | `403` |
| Rate limited | `429` |
| Unexpected failure | `500`, so the provider retries |

concepts.title: Core concepts
concepts.description: The eight ideas that explain how every RetAI screen behaves.
concepts.content:
Learn these once and the rest of the product stops surprising you.


  
Everything in RetAI belongs to exactly one clinic: patients, appointments, invoices, photos, messages, stock. A query can never reach across clinics, and there is no screen anywhere that shows two clinics' patients side by side.

Multi-location groups get one clinic record per location plus a group-owner account that can switch between them.
  

  
The phone number in E.164 format (`+919876543210`) is the identity key. It is what joins an inbound WhatsApp message, a voice call recording, an invoice, and a photo to the same person.

This is why the importer normalises numbers and why a manually typed number without a country code causes trouble later.
  

  
A **service** is one procedure at one price — a single laser session, a consultation, a peel.

A **package** is a bundle of sessions sold together — six laser sessions, valid twelve months, at a package price. RetAI tracks sessions consumed and sessions remaining, and recognises revenue against sessions delivered rather than all at once.

Sessions remaining is also the strongest signal in at-risk scoring: a patient with four paid sessions left who has not visited in ten weeks is the most valuable call your front desk can make today.
  

  
An appointment binds a patient, a service, a clinician, a room or resource, and a time. Creating one automatically:

- queues a reminder for the right moment before the slot
- pushes an event to the clinician's Google Calendar, if connected
- schedules a follow-up for after the visit
  

  
RetAI does not send messages the moment something happens. It writes a row into a follow-up queue with a trigger time, and a worker drains that queue every few minutes.

The consequence you care about: **a message is never sent twice.** Each queued item is claimed atomically before sending, so overlapping workers cannot double-message a patient. If bookkeeping fails *after* delivery, the row is parked for manual review rather than retried — a duplicate message to a patient is treated as worse than a missing log line.
  

  
Aisha is the reasoning layer between an inbound patient message and your calendar. She reads recent conversation, the patient's active treatment plan, and your live service catalogue, then either replies or calls a tool such as `book_appointment`.

Two guardrails are structural, not prompt-level:

- **Whose data she touches is never her decision.** The clinic and the patient come from the verified message sender on the server. A crafted message can influence what Aisha *says*; it cannot make her read another patient's record.
- **She cannot confirm what did not happen.** Replies claiming a booking that no tool actually made are intercepted before they reach the patient.
  

  
A ranking, not a label. It weighs time since last visit against that patient's own visit rhythm, unfinished package sessions, lifetime value, and treatment type. A quarterly-maintenance patient at eleven weeks is not at risk; a monthly patient at eleven weeks is.

The list is sorted by revenue at stake so the front desk works the most valuable call first.
  

  
Every dashboard screen is a **module**. Every role has a set of modules it may open. Owners always see everything and cannot be locked out of their own clinic.

Access is checked on the server when the page loads, not hidden in the browser — typing the URL of a module you lack access to gets you nothing.
  


## The daily loop, in one diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
A[Patient messagesWhatsApp] --> B{Aisha readshistory + catalogue}
B -->|answers| C[Reply sent]
B -->|books| D[Appointment created]
D --> E[Reminder queued]
D --> F[Google Calendar event]
E --> G[Patient attends]
G --> H[Consultation + Rx]
H --> I[Invoice + GST]
I --> J[Follow-up queued]
J --> K{Returns?}
K -->|no| L[At-risk list]
L --> M[AI win-back draft]
M --> A
K -->|yes| G
```

features/at-risk.title: At-Risk Patients
features/at-risk.description: Ranked list of patients drifting away, sorted by revenue at stake, with AI-drafted win-back messages.
features/at-risk.content:
This is the module the product is named after. Every clinic has patients quietly slipping away — a package half-finished, a maintenance cycle missed, a course of treatment abandoned after session two. They rarely announce it. They just stop coming.

## How the score works

At-risk is **a ranking, not a label.** It weighs:

| Signal | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Days since last visit, relative to *that patient's* own rhythm | A quarterly patient at 11 weeks is fine. A monthly patient at 11 weeks is not. |
| Sessions remaining on a paid package | Already-paid, unredeemed value is the easiest revenue in the clinic to recover. |
| Treatment type and expected cadence | Laser hair reduction has a biological interval. A missed one costs results, not just revenue. |
| Lifetime value | Two patients equally lapsed are not equally worth a phone call. |
| Recent no-shows or cancellations | A cancellation with no rebooking is a stronger drift signal than a long gap alone. |
| Open conversation state | A patient mid-conversation with Aisha is being handled; they do not need a second chase. |

The list is sorted by **revenue at stake**, so the top of the list is the most valuable call your front desk can make today — not merely the longest-absent name.

## Working the list


  
The list is recomputed continuously. Work top-down.
  
  
Every row states *why* it is there: "3 of 6 laser sessions remaining, 9 weeks since last visit, package expires in 41 days." You are never guessing at the pitch.
  
  
Click **Draft message**. RetAI writes a message grounded in that patient's real history — the treatment they had, the gap, what is unfinished.


You always see the draft before it goes. Edit freely. Send over WhatsApp with one click.
  
  
When the patient answers, Aisha handles the conversation and books the slot. The row leaves the at-risk list when the appointment is created.
  


## What the AI will and will not say

The drafting model is constrained. It may reference the patient's own treatment history, sessions remaining, and your published service catalogue.

It is forbidden from:

- Promising a clinical outcome or result timeline
- Inventing a discount, offer, or price not in your catalogue
- Claiming an appointment exists that has not been created
- Making any medical claim about the patient's condition


> **Note:** 
  Every AI-drafted message is logged with the context it was given. If a patient ever queries what your clinic told them, the record is complete.



## Bulk campaigns

Filter the list — for example *"package expiring within 30 days, sessions remaining"* — and send a personalised draft to everyone matching. Each message is generated per patient from their own history; this is not a mail merge with a name field.


> **Warning:** 
  Bulk sending is rate-limited and spread over time to protect your WhatsApp number's sending reputation. A hundred identical messages in one minute is how a business number gets restricted.



## Measuring recovery

The [Reports](#doc-features/reports) module tracks **revenue recovered** — bookings that came from an at-risk outreach, attributed to the message that produced them. That number is the honest measure of whether RetAI is paying for itself.


## Related


  

### [Win back a lapsed patient](#doc-workflows/win-back-a-lapsed-patient)
The end-to-end walkthrough.


  

### [WhatsApp Inbox](#doc-features/chats)
Where the replies land.

features/billing.title: Billing
features/billing.description: Point-of-sale checkout, per-line GST, split payments, invoice PDFs, and WhatsApp delivery.
features/billing.content:
## Checkout


  
Or start from an appointment, which pre-fills the patient and the service delivered.
  
  
Services, packages, retail products, or a free-text item for anything not in the catalogue. Quantities and per-line discounts are supported.
  
  
GST is calculated **per line at that line's own rate** and shown live. A bill mixing 5% and 18% items is never blended into a single wrong average rate.
  
  
One method or several — see split payments below.
  
  
The invoice number is allocated atomically from a per-clinic sequence. Two tills billing at the same instant cannot produce the same invoice number.
  


## Payment methods

Cash, card, UPI, bank transfer, cheque, package redemption, and clinic credit.

### Split payments

One invoice, several tenders — ₹5,000 on UPI and ₹3,000 in cash, say. Each part is recorded separately so your day-end reconciliation by method actually balances.


### Partial payment and outstanding

Take less than the full amount and the remainder is recorded as outstanding against the patient. Outstanding balances appear on the patient profile, in the day-end report, and in the overdue-accounts list.

## Invoice delivery


  

### WhatsApp
One click. The patient receives a link to the PDF. Delivery is logged on the patient's conversation.


  

### Download or print
A4 PDF on your letterhead with GSTIN, HSN/SAC codes, and the tax breakdown.




## Retainer and credit

Patients who pay in advance against future treatment hold a **retainer balance**. Refunds, goodwill adjustments, and overpayments create **clinic credit**. Both are redeemable at checkout and both appear on the patient profile, so the front desk cannot miss that a patient already has money on account.

## Invoice list and search

Filter by date range, patient, payment method, staff member, service, or outstanding status. Export any filtered view to CSV for your accountant — see [Data export](#doc-admin/data-export).

## Day-end close

The day-end report reconciles: total collected by method, invoices issued, discounts granted with who granted them, refunds, outstanding created, and GST collected by rate.


> **Tip:** 
  Run day-end before the last person leaves, not the next morning. A discrepancy is trivially traceable while the person who took the payment is still in the building.



See [Month-end close](#doc-workflows/month-end-close) for the monthly version.

## Amendments, refunds, and cancellation

Issued invoices are not silently editable — they are tax documents.

| Action | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Amend** | Creates a revision. Both versions are kept and linked. |
| **Refund** | Recorded against the original invoice with a reason. |
| **Cancel** | The invoice is voided, not deleted. It stays in the sequence and in reports. |


> **Warning:** 
  Refunds and cancellations require billing permission and are audited with the staff member's name. This is a control, not an inconvenience.



## A known limitation, stated plainly

Invoice creation writes the invoice, its line items, and the ledger entry as a sequence rather than as a single atomic transaction. In the rare event of an infrastructure failure mid-write, a partially built invoice can result. RetAI logs these and they are reconcilable, but we would rather you knew than discovered it.

## Related


  

### [Reports](#doc-features/reports)
Revenue, tax, and collection reporting.


  

### [Treatment Packages](#doc-features/packages)
Why package revenue is recognised over time.

features/calendar.title: AI Calendar
features/calendar.description: Multi-clinician scheduling with tentative holds, resource columns, drag-to-move, and two-way Google Calendar sync.
features/calendar.content:
The calendar is the busiest screen in the product. It is built for a clinic where four clinicians, two laser rooms, and a walk-in queue all compete for the same hour.

## Views


  

#### Day

One column per clinician or resource. The default working view for the front desk. Current time is marked with a live line.
  


  

#### Week

Seven days for one clinician, or a compressed all-clinician view. Use it for planning next week's capacity.
  


  

#### Month

Density heat map. Useful for spotting the quiet Tuesdays worth filling with a win-back campaign.
  


  

#### List

A flat chronological list — the fastest view on a phone, and the one to use when the front desk is calling through tomorrow's confirmations.
  




## Booking an appointment


  

##### Click an empty slot

Or click **New appointment** and pick the time.
  
  

##### Pick the patient

Search by name or phone number. If the patient does not exist, create them inline — name and phone are the only required fields.
  
  

##### Pick the service

The service's configured duration sets the slot length automatically. Override it if this particular case needs longer.
  
  

##### Pick the clinician

Only clinicians qualified for that service are offered. Configure that mapping in [Services](#doc-features/services).
  
  

##### Save

A reminder is queued, a follow-up is scheduled, and the event appears on the clinician's Google Calendar if connected.
  


## Appointment statuses

| Status | Meaning | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tentative | Held but unconfirmed. Does not block the slot for another booking. | Amber |
| Confirmed | Patient has confirmed, by reply or by phone. | Green |
| Checked in | Patient is in the clinic. | Blue |
| Completed | Visit finished. Triggers the post-visit follow-up. | Grey |
| No-show | Patient did not attend. Feeds at-risk scoring. | Red |
| Cancelled | Cancelled in advance. Frees the slot. | Muted |


> **Tip:** 
  **Tentative** is the status most clinics under-use. When a patient says "probably Thursday", hold it as tentative. It shows on the calendar, it does not block the slot, and the reminder system chases the confirmation for you.



## Moving and rescheduling

Drag an appointment to a new time or a different clinician's column. On save, RetAI:

1. Updates the record and the Google Calendar event
2. Cancels the old reminder and queues a new one
3. Optionally messages the patient with the new time — you are asked before it sends


> **Warning:** 
  Dragging an appointment into an occupied slot is allowed — clinics genuinely double-book on purpose. RetAI warns you, it does not block you. Aisha's automatic bookings, by contrast, never double-book.



## How the AI books into this calendar

When a patient asks Aisha for an appointment, she does not guess. She reads the service duration, the clinicians qualified for that service, and existing bookings, then offers real free slots. The appointment she creates is an ordinary appointment — same statuses, same reminders, same Google sync.


See [WhatsApp Inbox](#doc-features/chats) for the conversation side of this.

## Google Calendar sync

Two-way, per clinician:

- **Push** — an appointment created in RetAI appears on the clinician's Google Calendar within seconds
- **Pull** — personal events the clinician blocks out in Google appear in RetAI as busy time, so nothing gets booked over their lunch

Setup: [Connect Google Calendar](#doc-admin/integrations/google-calendar).

## Related


  

### [A day at the front desk](#doc-workflows/front-desk-day)
Where the calendar fits in the daily routine.


  

### [Services](#doc-features/services)
Durations and clinician mapping — the inputs the calendar relies on.

features/chats.title: WhatsApp Inbox
features/chats.description: Every patient conversation in one place, with Aisha answering questions and booking appointments on her own.
features/chats.content:
WhatsApp is where Indian clinics actually talk to patients. RetAI treats it as the primary channel, not a notification afterthought.

## The inbox

Threads sort by most recent message. Each thread shows the patient's name (or their number if they are not yet a patient), a preview, and an unread badge. Selecting a thread opens the conversation alongside that patient's context — active packages, last visit, upcoming appointment, outstanding balance.

Filters: **Unread**, **Needs attention**, **Handled by AI**, **Assigned to me**.

## Aisha — what she does unprompted

When a patient messages, Aisha reads the recent conversation, that patient's active treatment plan, and your live service catalogue. Then she either replies or acts.


  

### Answers questions
What a treatment involves, what it costs, how long a session takes, what aftercare is required — all from your own catalogue, never invented.


  

### Books appointments
Finds a genuinely free slot with a qualified clinician for the requested service, and creates the appointment.


  

### Reschedules and cancels
Moves an existing booking and re-queues the reminder.


  

### Escalates
Anything clinical, any complaint, anything she is not confident about goes to a human and the thread is flagged **Needs attention**.




### What she will never do


> **Warning:** 
  These are enforced in code, not merely requested in a prompt:

  - **She cannot cross patients.** Which clinic and which patient a conversation belongs to is resolved on the server from the verified message sender. A crafted message can steer what Aisha *says*; it cannot make her read or write another patient's record.
  - **She cannot confirm a booking that was not made.** Replies claiming an appointment that no tool actually created are intercepted before they reach the patient.
  - **She cannot make clinical or outcome claims.** A forbidden-claims filter runs on every outgoing message.
  - **She cannot invent prices or offers.** Numbers come from your service catalogue.



## Taking over from the AI

Click **Take over** on any thread. Aisha stops replying to that conversation and it becomes yours. Your replies send under the same clinic number, so the patient sees one continuous conversation.

Click **Hand back** to return the thread to the AI.


> **Tip:** 
  Threads marked **Needs attention** are the ones Aisha deliberately did not answer. Working that filter first is the fastest way to keep the inbox honest.



## Templates and quick replies

For the messages you send constantly — directions to the clinic, pre-procedure instructions, parking guidance — save a quick reply and insert it with two clicks. Templates support patient-name and appointment-time placeholders.

## Automatic messages

Beyond conversation, RetAI sends on its own:

| Message | When |
| --- | --- |
| Appointment reminder | Configurable, typically 24h and 2h before |
| Confirmation request | On tentative bookings |
| Post-visit follow-up | After a completed appointment |
| Aftercare instructions | On procedures configured to send them |
| Package session reminder | When sessions remain and the gap is growing |
| Invoice delivery | On demand from [Billing](#doc-features/billing) |
| Win-back | From [At-Risk Patients](#doc-features/at-risk) |

Timing rules are set in [Clinic setup](#doc-admin/clinic-setup).

## Delivery and duplicates

Every message is logged with its delivery status. Two properties are worth knowing:

- **Nothing sends twice.** Queued messages are claimed atomically before sending, so overlapping workers cannot double-message a patient.
- **Inbound messages are deduplicated at the database level.** WhatsApp retries a webhook on any hiccup; a retried delivery cannot produce a second reply from Aisha.

## Related


  

### [Connect WhatsApp](#doc-admin/integrations/whatsapp)
Setup and number verification.


  

### [Mobile app](#doc-features/mobile)
Push notifications when a patient messages.

features/consultations.title: Consultations & Rx
features/consultations.description: Form-based consultation templates, an anatomical drawing tool, and prescription templates for derma and aesthetic practice.
features/consultations.content:
Free-text notes are unsearchable and unauditable. RetAI consultations are structured forms, built per specialty, that still let a clinician draw exactly what they saw.


> **Note:** 
  Prescribing is off for the receptionist role by default. An owner can grant it in [Roles & permissions](#doc-admin/roles-and-permissions).



## Consultation templates

Each template is a set of fields your clinic defines: presenting complaint, history, examination findings, diagnosis, plan, and any specialty sections you need — Fitzpatrick type, hair-loss grade, acne severity, prior treatments, contraindications.


  

### Structured means searchable
"Every patient with Fitzpatrick IV who had a Q-switched session in the last year" is a filter, not an afternoon of reading notes.


  

### Templates per specialty
Derma, trichology, cosmetic surgery, and aesthetics ship as starting points. We customise them to your protocols during [onboarding](#doc-onboarding).




## The clinical drawing tool

Some findings are faster drawn than described. The annotation canvas gives the clinician a clean anatomical base diagram to mark on.


**Base diagrams available:**

| Diagram | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Face — front | Injectables, peels, lesion mapping |
| Face — three-quarter | Profile-dependent work, jawline, temple |
| Scalp — vertex | Hair-loss grading, graft planning, PRP sites |
| Body — front | Laser hair reduction areas, body contouring |

The diagrams are deliberately minimal line art — every line the diagram contributes is a line competing with the clinician's own marks. Landmarks appear only where they are needed to place an annotation accurately.

**Tools:** freehand pen, straight line, shaded region, point marker with a numbered label, text callout, and colour selection for distinguishing planned versus completed sites.


> **Tip:** 
  All diagrams share one coordinate space. Switching the base diagram — face front to three-quarter, say — does not invalidate marks already recorded. Annotations from successive visits can be overlaid to show progression.



## Prescriptions


  
Your common regimens — acne protocol, post-laser aftercare, melasma maintenance — saved with drugs, strengths, frequency, duration, and instructions already filled in.
  
  
Every field is editable. Allergies and clinical flags from the patient record are shown while you prescribe, not buried a tab away.
  
  
The prescription carries your clinic letterhead, the prescriber's name and registration number, and the date.
  
  
Print, download as PDF, or send to the patient over WhatsApp. Delivery is logged on the patient record.
  


### Pharmacy fulfilment

If you run an in-house pharmacy, a prescription can be dispensed against [Inventory](#doc-features/inventory) — stock is deducted and the items are added to the invoice.

## Aftercare instructions

Attach pre- and post-procedure instructions to any service. They send automatically at the right time relative to the appointment: pre-care the day before, aftercare an hour after the visit completes.


> **Warning:** 
  Consultation notes and prescriptions are clinical records. They are versioned and audited — edits are recorded with who and when, and nothing is silently overwritten. See [Retention & deletion](#doc-security/retention-and-deletion) for how long they are kept.



## Related


  

### [Before & After](#doc-features/gallery)
Photographs taken at the same visit, bound to the session.


  

### [Consultation to invoice](#doc-workflows/consultation-to-invoice)
The full clinical-to-commercial walkthrough.

features/gallery.title: Before & After
features/gallery.description: A consent-gated clinical photo library with watermarking, identity masking, and automatic session linkage.
features/gallery.content:
Before-and-after photographs are the strongest sales asset an aesthetic clinic owns and the most sensitive data it holds. RetAI treats them as both.

## Capturing photos


  
Photos can be captured from the patient profile, or directly from a package session so the linkage is automatic.
  
  
Use the device camera — the mobile app makes this a one-tap job at the chair — or upload from a DSLR.
  
  
Treatment, body area, angle (front, three-quarter, left, right), and whether it is a *before*, *progress*, or *after* image.
  
  
Two separate permissions, captured separately:

- **Clinical record** — always required. The photo is part of the medical record.
- **Marketing use** — optional and explicit. Without it, the photo is structurally incapable of entering a shareable collection.
  



> **Warning:** 
  Marketing consent is not a display setting that someone can toggle off later. A photo without recorded marketing consent cannot be added to a shareable collection at all — the export path refuses it. This is deliberate: under India's DPDP Act, "we forgot to blur it" is not a defence.



## Comparison view

Select any two images of the same patient and area to open a side-by-side or slider comparison, with the date and session number on each. Because photos bind to the package session they were taken at, before/after pairs assemble themselves rather than needing manual curation.


## Editing tools


  
Align a follow-up photo to the framing of the original so the comparison is honest.
  
  
Applies your logo at a configured position and opacity. Set it once in [Clinic setup](#doc-admin/clinic-setup) and it applies to every exported image.
  
  
Blur or bar the eyes and any identifying marks. On any export where marketing consent covers the treatment area but not facial identity, masking is required before the export completes.
  
  
Mark treatment sites or areas of interest directly on the image. Annotations are stored as a layer, so the original is never altered.
  


## Search and filters

Filter by treatment, body area, clinician, date range, consent state, and whether a matching after-photo exists. The last one is the useful one: **"before photos with no after photo"** is a list of patients who did not finish their course.

## Collections

Group images into a collection — "Laser hair reduction results", "Acne scar revision" — for use in counselling. Collections can be shown to a prospective patient on a tablet during consultation, or exported.


> **Note:** 
  Every image in a collection must carry marketing consent. Attempting to add one that does not is refused with the reason stated, not silently skipped.



## Storage and access

Photographs are stored encrypted, scoped to your clinic, and served only through short-lived signed URLs to signed-in staff. A URL copied from the browser expires and becomes useless — it cannot be forwarded as a permanent link.

## Related


  

### [Treatment Packages](#doc-features/packages)
Session linkage, which is what makes pairing automatic.


  

### [Data protection](#doc-security/data-protection)
Consent, encryption, and deletion of clinical images.

features/inventory.title: Inventory
features/inventory.description: Consumables, per-procedure bill of materials, automatic stock deduction, and pharmacy fulfilment.
features/inventory.content:
Aesthetic clinics lose real money to stock they cannot account for — a vial short at the end of the month with no record of where it went. RetAI ties consumption to the procedure that consumed it.

## Products

Every stock item carries:

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Name and SKU | |
| Category | Consumable, injectable, retail, pharmacy |
| Unit | Vial, ml, piece, box — the unit you actually count in |
| Purchase and selling price | Selling price only applies to retail and pharmacy items |
| GST rate | Applied per line when sold |
| Reorder level | Triggers a low-stock alert |
| Expiry tracking | On for anything with a shelf life |
| Batch tracking | On for injectables and pharmacy items |

## Bill of materials

Attach consumables to a service and the quantity each session uses. When a session is delivered, stock is deducted automatically — no separate stock entry, and no month-end guesswork about where the vials went.


> **Tip:** 
  Set the bill of materials once, at onboarding, for your ten highest-volume procedures. That covers most of your consumption. Add the long tail later.



## Stock movements

Every change in quantity is a ledger entry with a reason and a person attached:

- **Purchase received** — against a vendor and purchase order
- **Consumed by procedure** — automatic, linked to the appointment
- **Dispensed to patient** — pharmacy or retail sale, linked to the invoice
- **Internal issue** — moved to another room or location
- **Adjustment** — physical count correction, reason required
- **Wastage** — breakage, contamination, expiry, reason required
- **Return to vendor**


> **Note:** 
  There is no way to change a quantity without leaving a ledger row. That is the entire point of the module.



## Vendors and purchase orders

Maintain vendor records with contact details and payment terms. Raise a purchase order, send it, receive against it — partially if that is what arrived — and stock updates on receipt. Outstanding POs and short deliveries are visible on the inventory overview.

## Expiry and batches

Batch-tracked items record batch number and expiry on receipt. Consumption is FIFO by expiry date, so the oldest stock goes first. Items approaching expiry surface on the overview at a threshold you set.


> **Warning:** 
  Expiry alerts depend on batch data being entered at receipt. Skipping it at the goods-in stage means no expiry warning later — the system cannot warn about a date nobody recorded.



## Prescription fulfilment

A prescription written in [Consultations & Rx](#doc-features/consultations) can be dispensed here: stock deducts, the items are added to the patient's invoice, and the dispensing is recorded against the prescription.

## Stock take

Enter counted quantities against system quantities. RetAI shows the variance per item and its value, and posts the adjustments as ledger entries with your stock-take reference.

## Reports

Consumption by procedure, consumption by clinician, stock value on hand, wastage rate, expiry write-offs, and reorder suggestions based on run rate.


> **Tip:** 
  **Consumption by clinician** is the report nobody asks for and everybody should read. Two clinicians doing the same procedure with materially different consumption is either a training issue or a leak.



## Related


  

### [Services](#doc-features/services)
Where the bill of materials is attached.


  

### [Billing](#doc-features/billing)
Selling retail and pharmacy items.

features/leads.title: Leads Pipeline
features/leads.description: Enquiries that are not yet patients — counselling notes, editable quotations, ownership, and follow-up.
features/leads.content:
An aesthetic clinic's real conversion problem is not the consultation — it is the fortnight after it, when a quoted patient goes quiet. The Leads module exists for that fortnight.

## Where leads come from

| Source | How it arrives |
| --- | --- |
| WhatsApp enquiry | An unknown number messages; Aisha handles it and creates the lead |
| Missed or answered call | The [AI Receptionist](#doc-features/receptionist) captures the enquiry |
| Walk-in | Reception creates it by hand |
| Website form | Via the API — see [CRM endpoints](#doc-api-reference/endpoints/crm) |
| Campaign import | CSV upload |

## Pipeline stages


  
Just arrived, no one has spoken to them yet. Unassigned leads are flagged.
  
  
Someone has spoken to them. Log what was discussed.
  
  
An appointment exists. The lead is linked to it.
  
  
A quotation has been issued. This is where deals sit longest and die quietest.
  
  
Treatment purchased. The lead becomes a patient record; nothing is retyped.
  
  
With a reason — price, timing, went elsewhere, no response. Lost reasons are the most useful report in this module.
  


## Counselling and quotations

The counselling tool is for the conversation where a patient asks "so what would all of this cost?"


  
Add services and packages, apply a discount, and RetAI computes GST per line at the correct rate for each item. Save it against the lead. Revise it as many times as the conversation needs — every version is kept.
  
  
Deliver as a branded PDF over WhatsApp or email. Delivery and open are logged against the lead.
  
  
Free-text counselling notes — concerns raised, budget signalled, objections. These are visible to whoever picks the lead up next, which is the entire point.
  
  
When the patient accepts, convert the quotation straight to a checkout. Nothing is re-entered, so the quoted price and the billed price cannot drift apart.
  


## Ownership and follow-up

Every lead has an owner and a next-action date. Overdue actions surface on the owner's overview screen and, if enabled, as a push notification.


> **Tip:** 
  Set the next-action date during the counselling conversation, while the patient is still in front of you. A lead with no next action is a lost lead with a delay.



## Reporting

The Leads report shows conversion by source, by owner, and by service; average days from enquiry to conversion; and the breakdown of lost reasons. See [Reports](#doc-features/reports).

## Related


  

### [Billing](#doc-features/billing)
Converting an accepted quotation.


  

### [Treatment Packages](#doc-features/packages)
What most quotations are actually for.

features/mobile.title: Mobile app
features/mobile.description: iOS and Android apps with push notifications for inbound patient messages.
features/mobile.content:
RetAI ships as native apps for iOS and Android in addition to the web app. Same account, same data, same permissions.

## What mobile is for


  

### Push on inbound messages
A patient messages after hours and the owner knows immediately. The notification is content-free by design — it tells you a message arrived, not what it said.


  

### Photo capture at the chair
Capture before/after images straight into the patient's session without a camera-to-computer transfer step.


  

### Calendar on the floor
Check the day, move an appointment, mark a patient checked in, without walking back to the desk.


  

### Patient lookup
Full patient record, history, and conversation, searchable by name or phone.




## Installing


  

#### iOS

Install from the App Store, open, and sign in with the same account you use on the web. Allow notifications when prompted — without that permission, inbound-message alerts do not arrive.
  


  

#### Android

Install from Google Play, open, and sign in. Allow notifications when prompted.
  




## Sign-in

Google sign-in and email/password both work. Google sign-in opens a secure system browser tab, completes with Google, and returns you to the app.


> **Warning:** 
  If Google sign-in returns to the app but leaves you on the login screen, your device is blocking the return redirect. Try disabling any VPN or content blocker for the sign-in, then retry. Persisting past that, see [Troubleshooting](#doc-help/troubleshooting).



## Notifications

Configure per device in **Settings → Notifications**:

| Notification | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Inbound patient WhatsApp message | On |
| Thread escalated by the AI | On |
| Appointment booked by the AI | Off |
| Overdue lead follow-up assigned to you | On |
| Low stock alert | Off — owners and managers only |
| Day-end report ready | Off |


> **Note:** 
  Push payloads never contain patient names or message content. Tapping the notification opens the app, which then loads the data under your authenticated session. A notification visible on a lock screen discloses nothing.



## Offline behaviour

The app requires a connection. It is a thin native shell around the same secure application the web serves, so there is no local copy of patient data on the device — and nothing to extract if the phone is lost.


> **Tip:** 
  That is a deliberate trade. Offline caching of clinical records on staff phones is a data-protection liability we chose not to create.

Enabling and troubleshooting notifications.

What most notifications are about.

| Module | Doctor | Receptionist |
