features/packages.title: Treatment Packages
features/packages.description: Multi-session packages with allocation, expiry, session tracking, and GST recognised on amount received.
features/packages.content:
Most aesthetic revenue is sold as a course, not a visit. Packages are where RetAI tracks the gap between money collected and treatment delivered — and that gap is where both your tax exposure and your retention risk live.

## Defining a package


  
A package is a set of services with a session count each. "Laser hair reduction — full legs × 6" or a mixed course: "4 × HydraFacial + 2 × chemical peel".
  
  
What the package is advertised at.
  
  
How long the patient has to use it. Expiry drives the reminders that recover unredeemed sessions.
  
  
The recommended gap between sessions. This is what tells RetAI a patient is falling behind their own course.
  


Pre-built package templates for common derma and aesthetic courses ship with the product; clone one and adjust rather than starting blank.

## Selling a package

At checkout, the counsellor can apply a discount. RetAI keeps four numbers distinct, and conflating them is the single most common accounting error in clinic software:

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **List price** | What the package is advertised at |
| **Discount** | Reduction granted by the counsellor |
| **Agreed price** | What the patient actually owes — list price minus discount |
| **Amount received** | What the clinic has actually collected so far |

From these RetAI derives:


  

### Earned value
The portion of the agreed price attributable to sessions actually delivered. This is revenue.


  

### Unearned advance
Money collected for sessions not yet delivered. This is a **liability** — the clinic owes treatment for it.


  

### Delivered unpaid
Treatment given that has not been paid for. The number clinic managers need and rarely have.


  

### Outstanding
Agreed price minus amount received.




## GST on amount received


> **Note:** 
  A six-session package sold today is **not** six sessions of revenue today, and it is **not** six sessions of GST liability today.



RetAI recognises tax against sessions delivered and money received rather than declaring the whole package at the point of sale. GST is computed **per line at that line's own rate**, so a package mixing a 5% item and an 18% item is not blended into a single wrong average.

The practical effect: your tax outflow tracks your actual delivery rather than running months ahead of it.


> **Warning:** 
  Package tax treatment depends on your clinic's own registration and accounting method. Configure it with your accountant during [onboarding](#doc-onboarding) — RetAI computes correctly under the method you set, but it does not choose the method for you.



## Allocating and scheduling sessions

From a sold package, allocate sessions to dates in one pass. RetAI proposes dates using the configured interval; adjust anything, then confirm. Each allocated session becomes an ordinary appointment on the [calendar](#doc-features/calendar) with its own reminder.


## Delivering a session

Marking a session delivered:

1. Increments sessions completed and recomputes earned value
2. Deducts consumables from [Inventory](#doc-features/inventory) via the procedure's bill of materials
3. Prompts for the session photograph, linked to that session number
4. Recognises the revenue and tax portion for the delivered session
5. Schedules the next session's reminder

## Expiry and recovery

Packages approaching expiry with sessions remaining are surfaced in three places: the package list, the patient profile, and the [at-risk list](#doc-features/at-risk) — where they rank high, because the patient has already paid.


> **Tip:** 
  Filter packages by *"expiring within 30 days, sessions remaining"* and send the whole list an AI-drafted reminder. It is the highest-return five minutes available in the product.



## Refunds and part-cancellation

Cancelling a package with sessions remaining computes the refundable amount as amount received minus earned value, with any adjustment your policy requires. The refund is recorded against the original invoice so the audit trail stays intact.

## Related


  

### [Sell and track a package](#doc-workflows/sell-and-track-a-package)
Step-by-step walkthrough.


  

### [Billing](#doc-features/billing)
Invoicing, split payments, and receipts.

features/patients.title: All Patients
features/patients.description: The complete patient record — visits, treatments, photos, invoices, messages, and consent state in one place.
features/patients.content:
## The patient list

Search by name, phone, or email. Filter by:

- **Status** — active, lapsed, at risk, new this month
- **Last visit** — a date range
- **Treatment** — everyone who has ever had a specific procedure
- **Package state** — has sessions remaining, expiring soon, expired unused
- **Assigned clinician**


> **Tip:** 
  "Package expiring within 30 days with sessions remaining" is the highest-converting filter in the product. Those patients have already paid; they just need reminding.



## The patient profile

Every profile has the same tabs.


  
Contact details, date of birth, allergies and clinical flags, referral source, assigned clinician, lifetime value, and visit count. Clinical flags are pinned to the top of every tab — an allergy should not be something you have to go looking for.
  

  
Every past and upcoming appointment with service, clinician, status, and outcome. No-shows are marked; they feed at-risk scoring.
  

  
Active packages with sessions used and remaining, expiry dates, and the schedule of remaining sessions. Completed packages stay for history.
  

  
Before and after images bound to the session they were taken at, so the comparison is automatic rather than a manual curation chore. Marketing consent state is shown on every photo. See [Before & After](#doc-features/gallery).
  

  
Consultation notes from your clinic's templates, annotated diagrams, and every prescription issued, each downloadable as a PDF.
  

  
Every invoice, what was paid, what is outstanding, and the payment methods used. Retainer and credit balances show here.
  

  
The full WhatsApp thread, including every message Aisha sent on your behalf, and voice-call transcripts and outcomes. One timeline, one record of what the clinic said to this patient.
  


## Editing a patient

Click **Edit** on the overview tab. Changes are audited — who changed what and when is recorded.


> **Warning:** 
  Changing a phone number rebinds that patient's WhatsApp identity. Existing message history stays attached, but future messages from the old number will no longer match this patient. Change it only when the patient has genuinely changed number.



## Merging duplicates

Duplicates happen — a patient messages from a second number, or reception creates a second record for a walk-in.


  
  
  

##### Search for the duplicate and confirm

Visits, invoices, photos, packages, and messages move to the surviving record. The duplicate is archived, not deleted, so the audit trail survives.
  


## Downloadable patient summary

**Actions → Download summary** produces a PDF with demographics, treatment history, active packages, and outstanding balance — the document to hand a patient who asks for their records, or to attach to a referral.


> **Note:** 
  Patients have a right to their data under India's DPDP Act. This is the button that satisfies it. See [Data protection](#doc-security/data-protection).



## Related


  

### [At-Risk Patients](#doc-features/at-risk)
Which of these patients is drifting away, and what to send them.


  

### [Data import](#doc-admin/data-import)
Bringing your existing patient list in.

features/receptionist.title: AI Receptionist
features/receptionist.description: A voice agent that answers the calls your front desk misses, captures the enquiry, and logs it to the patient record.
features/receptionist.content:
Every missed call at an aesthetic clinic is a patient who called a competitor next. The AI Receptionist answers on the lines your team cannot get to — after hours, during procedures, or when both handsets are already busy.

## What a call looks like


  
Either every call, or only calls that ring unanswered past a threshold. Your choice — see [Voice setup](#doc-admin/integrations/voice).
  
  
If the number matches an existing patient, the agent knows their history. If not, it treats them as a new enquiry.
  
  
Clinic hours and location, what a treatment involves and costs, availability, and appointment booking or rescheduling.
  
  
Anything clinical, any complaint, or any request it cannot complete is handed off — transferred live if a human is available, otherwise captured as a callback with a summary.
  
  
Recording, transcript, outcome, and any created appointment are written to the patient's record.
  


## The call log

Each row shows caller, duration, outcome, and attributed patient. Open a call for:

- **Transcript** — full text, searchable
- **Recording** — audio playback, subject to your retention setting
- **Outcome** — booked, enquiry captured, escalated, or no action
- **Linked records** — appointments and leads created by the call


> **Note:** 
  A call's clinic and patient are resolved from the phone number on the server, never from the call payload. A spoofed or malformed payload cannot attribute a call to the wrong clinic.



## Outbound calls

Trigger a call from a patient record — confirmation for tomorrow's slot, a win-back for a lapsed high-value patient, or a package-expiry reminder. Outbound calling is rate-limited per clinic.


> **Warning:** 
  Recording consent is your clinic's legal obligation. RetAI plays a configurable consent announcement at call start; you are responsible for the wording matching what your jurisdiction requires. See [Data protection](#doc-security/data-protection).



## Configuring the agent

In [Voice setup](#doc-admin/integrations/voice) you control:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Greeting | The first line the caller hears |
| Voice and language | Including Indian English and regional language options |
| Answer policy | All calls, after-hours only, or overflow only |
| Escalation number | Where live transfers go |
| Booking permission | Whether the agent may create appointments or only capture enquiries |
| Recording retention | How long audio is kept before automatic deletion |


> **Tip:** 
  Start with **overflow only** and **enquiry capture, no booking**. Read a week of transcripts, tune the greeting and the treatment descriptions, then let it book. Clinics that turn everything on at once end up distrusting the transcripts they never read.



## When voice is not enabled

Voice is a separate tier. If your plan does not include it, the module is hidden and no calls are answered — the rest of RetAI is unaffected.

## Related


  

### [Voice setup](#doc-admin/integrations/voice)
Numbers, routing, and agent configuration.


  

### [Leads Pipeline](#doc-features/leads)
Where captured enquiries go.

features/reports.title: Reports
features/reports.description: Revenue, recovery, procedure mix, follow-up performance, demographics, and the day-end close.
features/reports.content:
Every report shares the same controls: a date range, a clinician filter, a service or category filter, and an **Export CSV** button. Nothing is a dead end.

## Revenue


  
Collected versus billed, by day, week, or month. Split by payment method, service category, and clinician. Package revenue appears as it is earned, not as it is collected — see [Packages](#doc-features/packages).
  
  
Tax collected by rate, with taxable value per rate. The report your accountant asks for.
  
  
Who owes what, bucketed by age. Sorted by amount so the calls worth making are at the top.
  
  
Every discount with the staff member who granted it. Discount as a percentage of gross is the number to watch.
  
  
Advance money held and credit outstanding. Both are liabilities, and both are easy to forget.
  


## Retention — the reports that justify the product


  

### Revenue recovered
Bookings that came from an at-risk outreach, attributed to the message that produced them. The honest measure of RetAI's return.


  

### Follow-up performance
Messages sent, replied to, and converted to a booking — by message type and by timing.


  

### Retention rate
Share of patients returning within their expected interval, trended over time.


  

### Package completion
Share of sold sessions actually delivered. Unredeemed sessions are a liability and a retention failure at once.




## Clinical and operational

| Report | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| Appointments overview | Booked, completed, cancelled, no-show — by day, clinician, and service |
| No-show analysis | Who, when, which slots, and whether reminders were delivered |
| Procedure trends | Which treatments are growing and which are fading, period over period |
| Clinician utilisation | Booked hours against available hours |
| Chair and room utilisation | Where the physical bottleneck actually is |
| Patient demographics | Age, gender, location, referral source |
| New versus returning | New patient acquisition against returning volume |
| Feedback analytics | Post-visit ratings and comments, by clinician and service |
| Incentive payouts | Staff commission based on your configured rules |
| Consumption by procedure | From [Inventory](#doc-features/inventory) |

## Day-end report

The close-of-business reconciliation: collections by method, invoices issued, discounts, refunds, outstanding created, GST collected by rate, and appointments completed against booked.


> **Tip:** 
  Run it before the last person leaves. A ₹500 discrepancy is trivially traceable while the person who took the payment is still there, and near-impossible three days later.



## Scheduled reports

Any report can be scheduled to arrive by email or WhatsApp on a cadence — day-end nightly to the owner, revenue summary every Monday, package expiry every Friday.


## Exports

Every report exports to CSV. A full clinic export — patients, appointments, invoices, and treatments in one archive — is available to owners from [Data export](#doc-admin/data-export).

## Related


  

### [Month-end close](#doc-workflows/month-end-close)
The monthly routine, in order.


  

### [At-Risk Patients](#doc-features/at-risk)
Where recovered revenue originates.

features/services.title: Services
features/services.description: Your procedure catalogue — price, GST rate, duration, clinician mapping, and consumables.
features/services.content:
The service catalogue is the smallest module and the one everything else depends on. The calendar, the AI agent, billing, inventory, and packages all read from it.

## Fields on a service

| Field | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| **Name** | What appears on the invoice and what Aisha calls it to patients |
| **Category** | Groups the catalogue — Laser, Injectables, Facials, Consultation, Trichology |
| **Price** | Base price before any package or discount |
| **GST rate** | Per service, not per clinic. Applied per line at billing. |
| **Duration** | Sets the slot length on the calendar and constrains what the AI can offer |
| **Clinicians** | Who may deliver it. The calendar and the AI both respect this. |
| **Consumables** | Bill of materials deducted from stock on delivery |
| **Pre/post care** | Instructions sent automatically around the appointment |
| **Patient-facing description** | What Aisha tells a patient who asks what this treatment involves |


> **Warning:** 
  Duration and clinician mapping are load-bearing. A wrong duration produces double-booked chairs; a missing clinician mapping means the AI cannot offer that service at all, and patients asking for it get escalated instead of booked.



## The patient-facing description

This field is what Aisha reads when a patient asks "what is a HydraFacial?" or "how long does laser take?". Write it as you would say it to a patient.


> **Tip:** 
  Include what the session involves, how long it takes, roughly what to expect afterwards, and the price. Leave out anything you would not want stated without a consultation — outcome promises, in particular. Aisha will not invent claims, but she will faithfully repeat one you wrote.



## Categories and ordering

Categories control grouping on the checkout screen and in reports. Order services within a category so your highest-volume items are first — the front desk is picking from this list forty times a day.

## Price changes

Editing a price affects future invoices only. Existing invoices and sold packages keep the price they were sold at; historical revenue never restates.


> **Note:** 
  Sold packages hold their own agreed price. Raising the price of a component service does not change what an existing package holder owes.



## Bulk import

Long price lists come in by CSV — name, category, price, GST rate, duration. See [Data import](#doc-admin/data-import).

## Related


  

### [Inventory](#doc-features/inventory)
Attaching consumables to a service.


  

### [Treatment Packages](#doc-features/packages)
Bundling services into a course.

features/staff.title: Staff
features/staff.description: Team accounts, roles, the per-module permission matrix, and de-provisioning.
features/staff.content:
> **Note:** 
  The Staff module is visible to **owners only** by default, and cannot be granted to a receptionist role. A clinic should not be able to lock out its own administrator.



## Adding a staff member


  
Name, work email, phone, and role.
  
  
Owner, Doctor, or Receptionist. The role sets the default module access; you can override it per module afterwards.
  
  
For doctors: registration number, specialty, signature for prescriptions, and which services they may deliver.
  
  
They receive sign-in instructions. Google sign-in works immediately for the email you entered; there is no self-registration path, so an unrecognised Google account cannot create itself access.
  


## Roles

| Role | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| **Owner** | Every module, always. Cannot be restricted. Can manage staff, permissions, and clinic settings. |
| **Doctor** | Clinical and commercial modules. No staff management by default. |
| **Receptionist** | Front-of-house modules. No billing, inventory, or prescriptions by default. |

Full defaults are in the [module tour](#doc-features/overview).

## The permission matrix

Toggle any module on or off for the Doctor and Receptionist roles, per clinic. Changes take effect on the staff member's next page load.


> **Warning:** 
  Access is enforced on the server when a page loads, not hidden in the browser. Typing the URL of a module you lack access to returns nothing. Do not rely on "they don't know the URL" — but equally, do not worry that they might.



## Clinician availability

Set working days, hours, breaks, and leave per clinician. This constrains the calendar and constrains what the AI agent can offer — a slot outside a clinician's hours will not be booked by Aisha.


## Presence

The staff list shows who is currently signed in and active. Useful at a busy front desk for knowing who can pick up an escalated WhatsApp thread right now.

## De-provisioning

Deactivate a staff member and their access ends. Two properties are worth knowing:

- **Their session does not survive.** Role and clinic are re-read from the staff record periodically, so a removed staff member loses access within minutes — they cannot ride out the remaining lifetime of an already-issued session.
- **Their records survive.** Consultations, invoices, and messages they created stay attached to their name. Clinical and financial history does not disappear because someone left.


> **Tip:** 
  Deactivate, do not delete. Deletion of a staff member who has ever signed a prescription would orphan a clinical record.



## Audit

Sign-ins, permission changes, discount grants, refunds, record edits, and data exports are logged with the staff member and timestamp. See [Access control](#doc-security/access-control).

## Related


  

### [Roles & permissions](#doc-admin/roles-and-permissions)
The full configuration guide.


  

### [Access control](#doc-security/access-control)
How access is enforced, not just configured.

help/changelog.title: Changelog
help/changelog.content:
## WhatsApp AI as the primary patient channel

  Aisha now handles the full conversation — answering treatment questions from your live catalogue, offering genuinely free slots, and creating the appointment herself. Bookings she makes are ordinary appointments with the same reminders and calendar sync as any other.

  ## Clinical drawing tool

  Annotate findings directly on anatomical base diagrams: face front, face three-quarter, scalp vertex, and body front. All diagrams share one coordinate space, so switching the base diagram does not invalidate existing marks and annotations from successive visits can be overlaid.

  **Also in this release**
  - Escalation flagging in the WhatsApp inbox for threads the AI deliberately did not answer
  - Take over / hand back on individual conversations



  ## Before & After photo library

  Consent-gated clinical image library with watermarking, identity masking, and automatic linkage to package sessions — so before/after pairs assemble themselves instead of being curated by hand.

  Marketing consent is structural: a photo without it cannot enter a shareable collection at all.

  ## Treatment packages

  Multi-session packages with allocation, expiry, session tracking, and revenue recognised against sessions delivered rather than declared at point of sale. List price, discount, agreed price, and amount received are tracked as four distinct numbers.

  ## Prescription templates

  Reusable regimens with drugs, strengths, frequency, and instructions pre-filled. Issue as PDF, print, or deliver over WhatsApp.



  ## Per-line GST

  GST is now computed per line at each line's own rate. A bill mixing 5% and 18% items is no longer blended into a single average rate.

  

> **Warning:** 
This corrected an under-declaration on mixed-rate invoices. If your clinic issued mixed-rate invoices before this release, review them with your accountant.
  



  ## Structural route guards

  A test suite now sweeps every API route and dashboard page for its authentication guard and session-derived clinic scoping. Adding a route that forgets either one fails the build.

  ## Atomic invoice numbering

  Invoice numbers are allocated from a row-locked per-clinic sequence. Concurrent checkouts cannot collide.

  ## Published architecture and known limitations

  The [architecture](#doc-security/architecture) and [known limitations](#doc-security/architecture) pages are now public.



  - Multi-tenant clinic isolation with row-level security as an independent second layer
  - NextAuth sessions with Google sign-in and no self-registration
  - Two-way Google Calendar sync with AES-256-GCM encrypted token storage
  - Bolna AI voice receptionist with server-side call attribution
  - Follow-up queue with atomic claiming — no message can send twice
  - GST invoicing with split payments and WhatsApp invoice delivery
  - Inventory with per-procedure bill of materials and automatic deduction
  - At-risk scoring with AI-drafted win-back messages
  - iOS and Android apps with content-free push notifications

help/faq.title: FAQ
help/faq.description: The questions clinics actually ask, answered honestly.
help/faq.content:
## The AI


  
Aisha does not pretend to be a named human. Configure her introduction to state she is the clinic's assistant — most clinics do, and patients respond well to it. What matters more in practice is that she answers accurately and books correctly.
  
  
No, and it is prevented from doing so. Clinical questions are escalated to a human and the thread is flagged. A claims filter blocks medical and outcome claims on every outgoing message.
  
  
It books into real free slots with clinicians qualified for the service, so structurally wrong bookings are rare. Anything it does book is an ordinary appointment you can move or cancel. Start with booking permission off and enable it once you have read a week of conversations.
  
  
Yes — entirely, or per conversation with **Take over**. The rest of RetAI works exactly as before.
  
  
No. Which clinic and which patient a conversation belongs to is resolved on the server from the verified sender, before the model is involved. A crafted message can influence what the AI says; it cannot change whose record it reads. See [Architecture](#doc-security/architecture).
  
  
English and major Indian languages, including code-mixed messages — which is how most patients actually write. Configure the primary language in clinic settings.
  


## WhatsApp


  
Yes, provided it is not currently registered on the WhatsApp consumer or Business app. Migrating it means that app stops working for that number. Most clinics take a fresh number and forward the old one.
  
  
Only if you use it badly. RetAI rate-limits sends, spreads bulk campaigns over time, respects quiet hours, and honours opt-outs permanently. The fastest way to damage a number is a mass blast of near-identical promotional messages — which is why the [at-risk flow](#doc-features/at-risk) personalises per patient instead.
  
  
WhatsApp allows pre-approved templates any time, but free-form conversation only within 24 hours of the patient's last message. RetAI uses templates for reminders and win-backs, and natural conversation inside the open window.
  
  
Both come from your clinic number as one continuous conversation. Taking over a thread is seamless from the patient's side.
  


## Data and migration


  
Yes. Send whatever format you have — CSV, Excel, even photographs of a printed price list. We validate, normalise, dedupe, dry-run into a demo tenant, then import live. See [Data import](#doc-admin/data-import).
  
  
Any time, without asking. Full clinic export in CSV plus a separate image archive. Available throughout your contract and for 30 days after it ends. See [Data export](#doc-admin/data-export).
  
  
No. Every record belongs to exactly one clinic and clinic identity comes from your session, never from a request. There is no screen anywhere that shows two clinics' patients together.
  
  
Database region is selected at project setup. Several subprocessors operate from the United States. All disclosed in [Subprocessors](#doc-security/subprocessors).
  
  
No. RetAI is built for the Indian market and the DPDP Act, and we hold no Business Associate Agreements. If you need HIPAA coverage we are not currently the right vendor.
  


## Billing and money


  
GST is computed **per line at that line's own rate** — a bill mixing 5% and 18% items is never blended into a single wrong average. Package revenue is recognised against sessions delivered rather than declared entirely at the point of sale.
  
  
Yes. One invoice, several tenders, each recorded separately so day-end reconciliation by method balances.
  
  
Not silently — it is a tax document. Amending creates a linked revision; both versions are kept. Cancellation voids rather than deletes.
  
  
Through CSV export today. Every report exports, and the full archive includes invoices, line items, payments, and the tax breakdown.
  


## Practical


  
Typically 7–10 working days from kickoff to go-live, mostly determined by how quickly your existing data reaches us. See [Onboarding](#doc-onboarding).
  
  
Two live online sessions, recorded for new joiners, plus a demo tenant to practise on before touching real records.
  
  
RetAI needs a connection. There is deliberately no offline copy of patient data on staff devices — offline caching of clinical records on phones is a liability we chose not to create. Keep a mobile hotspot as backup; most clinics do.
  
  
Yes, native apps for iOS and Android with push notifications. See [Mobile app](#doc-features/mobile).
  
  
Yes. One clinic record per location, plus a group-owner account that switches between them.

help/support.title: Support
help/support.description: How to reach us, what to include, and what to expect back.
help/support.content:
## How to reach us


  

### Your clinic WhatsApp group
**The fastest route.** Opened at onboarding and never closed. Your onboarding engineer is in it.


  

### Email
**support@retai.tech** — for anything needing a paper trail.


  

### Security
**security@retai.tech** — vulnerabilities and suspected data incidents. Acknowledged within one business day.


  

### [Status page](https://status.retai.tech)
Check here first if something looks broken across the whole product.




## Response targets

| Severity | Definition | Target first response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Critical** | Service completely unavailable | 1 hour |
| **High** | A core feature broken for your clinic — WhatsApp AI, billing, sign-in | 4 business hours |
| **Normal** | A non-core issue or question | 1 business day |
| **Low** | Feature request, general question | 3 business days |

Business hours are IST. Full terms: [Service levels](#doc-security/sla).

## What to include


  
The screen and the action. "Taking payment on the checkout screen."
  
  
"The invoice to show 18% GST on the serum."
  
  
"It showed 5%."
  
  
Invoice number, patient phone, appointment time. This is what turns a two-day exchange into a one-message fix.
  
  
Roughly is fine. It lets us find the request in the logs.
  
  
Almost always worth it.
  



> **Warning:** 
  Do not send patient names, photographs, or clinical details in a support message. Send the invoice number or the patient's internal reference instead — we can look up what we need from our side without you transmitting PHI over a support channel.



## Support access to your data

RetAI staff hold **no standing access** to your clinic's data after handover. Where a problem genuinely requires it, we ask in your WhatsApp group, access is time-boxed, and it is logged.


> **Tip:** 
  Ask to see that log any time. If a vendor cannot tell you exactly when their staff accessed your patient data, that answers a more important question than the one you asked.



## Training

- Two live sessions at onboarding, recorded for new joiners
- A demo tenant that stays available for practice
- Refresher sessions on request — useful when you hire

## Feature requests

Send them to the WhatsApp group or support@retai.tech. Tell us the **problem**, not only the feature — "the front desk forgets to rebook before the patient leaves" gets you a better answer than "add a rebook button".

Shipped changes appear in the [changelog](#doc-help/changelog).

help/troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
help/troubleshooting.description: The problems clinics actually hit, and how to fix them without waiting for support.
help/troubleshooting.content:
## Sign-in


  
Your staff record has not been created, or has been deactivated. This is a permissions problem, not a password problem — resetting the password will not help.

**Fix:** an owner adds or reactivates you in **Staff**.
  
  
The return redirect is being blocked, usually by a VPN, a content blocker, or strict cookie settings.

**Fix:** disable the VPN or blocker for sign-in, allow cookies for the site, then retry. On mobile this can also be an in-app browser — open in the system browser instead.
  
  
Sessions expire after 8 hours idle. Also expected if an owner has just changed your role or deactivated and reactivated your account.
  
  
An owner changed the permission matrix. Not a bug. Ask them, or see [Roles & permissions](#doc-admin/roles-and-permissions).
  


## WhatsApp


  
Phone-format mismatch. The patient record holds a number without a country code, so the inbound message does not match.

**Fix:** open the patient, correct the phone to full international format (`+919876543210`), save. History reattaches.

**Prevent:** always enter numbers with the country code. The bulk importer does this automatically; manual entry does not.
  
  
Most likely a staff member clicked **Take over** — a taken-over thread is deliberately silent from the AI.

**Fix:** click **Hand back** on the thread. If no takeover occurred, check the AI is enabled in clinic settings.
  
  
Check in this order:

1. Is the message template still approved?
2. Is the send time falling inside quiet hours?
3. Has this patient opted out?
4. Is the appointment status one that triggers a reminder — cancelled appointments do not remind

If all four are fine, check [status](https://status.retai.tech) for a delivery incident.
  
  
RetAI's queue claims each message atomically before sending, so genuine double-sends are prevented. A duplicate is almost always WhatsApp-side redelivery.

Report it with the patient's number and approximate time and we will check the delivery log.
  
  
Business verification is incomplete or the display name is pending WhatsApp review. This sits on WhatsApp's side; raise it with us and we chase it.
  


## Calendar


  
Usually the Google account changed password or revoked access.

**Fix:** Settings → Integrations → Google Calendar → Disconnect, then Connect again.
  
  
The events are on a different calendar in the same account. Only the selected calendar is read.

**Fix:** move them, or change the selected calendar in integration settings.
  
  
Two staff accounts connected to the same Google calendar. Disconnect one.
  
  
Almost always the service has no clinician mapped to it, so there is no one qualified to deliver it.

**Fix:** [Services](#doc-features/services) → open the service → assign clinicians. Also confirm the service has a duration set.
  


## Billing


  
Check the GST rate on each *service*, not on the clinic. Rates are per service and applied per line. Also check whether catalogue prices are entered GST-inclusive or exclusive in [clinic setup](#doc-admin/clinic-setup) — the setting changes how every price is interpreted.
  
  
Working as designed. Package revenue is recognised against **sessions delivered**, not the full amount at point of sale. The uncollected portion appears as unearned advance — a liability, not revenue. See [Packages](#doc-features/packages).
  
  
A cancelled invoice keeps its number — it is voided, not deleted. Gaps mean cancellations, and the cancelled invoices are visible in the invoice list with their reason.
  
  
Rare, and a known limitation: invoice writes are sequential rather than one atomic transaction, so an infrastructure failure mid-write can leave a partial record. These are logged and reconcilable.

**Fix:** report it with the invoice number. Do not re-issue until we have looked, or you will have two.
  


## Photos


  
Marketing consent is not recorded for it. This is the protection working, not a bug — a photo without marketing consent is structurally barred from any shareable collection.

**Fix:** obtain and record the patient's marketing consent, then retry.
  
  
Image URLs are short-lived and signed. They expire by design so a copied link cannot become a permanent public route to a clinical image.

**Fix:** share from within RetAI rather than pasting a URL.
  
  
They are not bound to package sessions. Capture from the session rather than from the patient profile and pairing becomes automatic.
  


## Mobile


  
In order: system notification permission for the app, then per-alert toggles in Settings → Notifications, then sign out and back in to re-register the device.
  
  
Battery optimisation is suspending background delivery. Exclude RetAI from battery optimisation in system settings.
  
  
RetAI requires a live connection and holds no offline copy. Check connectivity, then force-close and reopen.
  


## Still stuck


  

### [Contact support](#doc-help/support)
Your clinic WhatsApp group is the fastest route.


  

### [Check status](https://status.retai.tech)
Live incidents and history.





> **Tip:** 
  When reporting, include: what you did, what you expected, what happened, the patient or invoice reference, and roughly when. That turns a two-day exchange into a one-message fix.

integration/README.title: integration/README
integration/README.content:
# Wiring the docs into the live landing site

## The shape of it

Mintlify hosts the documentation itself. It is **not** a React component you can
mount inside the Next app — it is a separate site on its own subdomain. So the
work on the landing site is two things:

1. A DNS record pointing `docs.retai.tech` at Mintlify
2. Links into it from the header, the footer, and the product page

`DocsEntry.tsx` in this directory is the second part, ready to paste.

```
www.retai.tech          →  landing site (your marketing repo)
docs.retai.tech         →  this Mintlify site
app / www.retai.tech    →  the RetAI application (this repo, main branch)
```

---

## 1. DNS

In the Mintlify dashboard: **Settings → Custom domain → `docs.retai.tech`**.
It gives you a CNAME. Add it at your DNS provider:

| Type | Name | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CNAME | `docs` | *(the value Mintlify shows you)* |

Propagation is usually minutes. Mintlify issues the TLS certificate itself.

---

## 2. Drop in the component

Copy `DocsEntry.tsx` into the landing repo at
`src/components/marketing/DocsEntry.tsx`.

It exports four pieces, each independently usable:

| Export | Where it goes |
| --- | --- |
| `DocsNavLink` | Header nav, beside Product and Pricing |
| `DocsFooterColumn` | Footer, as a "Resources" column |
| `DocsPromoSection` | Product page, below the feature sections |
| `DocsSupportStrip` | Just above the footer on any page |

```tsx
import {
  DocsNavLink,
  DocsFooterColumn,
  DocsPromoSection,
  DocsSupportStrip,
} from "@/components/marketing/DocsEntry";
```

### Dependencies

`lucide-react` and Tailwind. Both are already in this repo's `package.json`; if
the landing site is a separate project, confirm it has them.

### Colours

The component reads the brand CSS variables from `globals.css`
(`--brand-green`, `--olive-500`, `--surface-raised`, `--text-main`,
`--text-secondary`). Each has a literal fallback baked in, so it renders
correctly even in a project that does not share that stylesheet — but it will
look properly on-brand where it does.

---

## 3. Reciprocal links

Already configured in `docs.json`, so the two sites point at each other:

- Navbar button **Open RetAI** → `https://www.retai.tech`
- Global anchor **Main site** → `https://www.retai.tech`
- Logo click → `https://www.retai.tech`
- Footer columns → pricing, support, feature tour

Check those URLs resolve on your landing site before publishing. A docs footer
linking to a 404 is worse than no footer link.

---

## 4. If you would rather not use a subdomain

Two alternatives, both worse for a reason worth knowing:

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| `retai.tech/docs` via a Next.js rewrite proxying Mintlify | Keeps one domain and consolidates SEO, but you now own a proxy in the request path and Mintlify's previews and search can behave oddly behind it. |
| Rebuild the docs as MDX pages inside the Next app | Full control, no third party — and you have just taken on building search, navigation, versioning, dark mode, and an AI assistant that Mintlify gives you for nothing. |

The subdomain is the right default. Take one of the alternatives only if you
have a concrete reason, not for tidiness.

---

## 5. Before you point the domain

Work through `../REVIEW-BEFORE-PUBLISH.md` first. There are placeholder contact

including a support phone number that is currently a placeholder taken from a
competitor's site.

onboarding.title: Onboarding plan
onboarding.description: The 10-step programme RetAI runs with your clinic, from first call to go-live and beyond.
onboarding.content:
Clinic software fails at rollout, not at build. RetAI onboarding is a guided programme run by our team with yours — you are never handed a login and left to work it out.

**Typical duration: 7–10 working days** from kickoff to going live, depending on how quickly your existing patient data reaches us.


  
We open a WhatsApp group with your clinic owner, front-desk lead, and the RetAI onboarding engineer. Every question during rollout goes here — no ticket queues, no waiting for email.

This group stays open permanently. It becomes your support channel after go-live.
  

  
We collect, in one pass:

- Clinic logo, letterhead, registration and GSTIN details
- Staff list with roles and the modules each should see
- Service and procedure catalogue with prices, GST rates, and durations
- Package definitions — sessions, validity, price
- Existing patient records and visit history
- Consumables and stock, if you want inventory tracked from day one


> **Tip:** 
Whatever format you already have works — an Excel sheet, a CSV export from your current software, even photographs of a printed price list. We normalise it. See [Data import](#doc-admin/data-import) for the fields that matter.


  

  
Our engineer configures your tenant:

- Clinic record, branding, and invoice template
- Service catalogue, GST rates, package structures
- Consultation and prescription templates for your specialty
- Role permissions matrix
- Follow-up and reminder timing rules
- The AI agent's persona, tone, and the claims it is forbidden from making


> **Note:** 
Your data sits in its own tenant from the first row written. See [Architecture](#doc-security/architecture) for how clinic isolation is enforced.


  

  
Two online sessions, recorded so new joiners can watch them later:

| Session | Audience | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Front desk | Reception, coordinators | Calendar, patients, WhatsApp inbox, packages, billing |
| Clinical & owner | Doctors, owner | Consultations, Rx, photo library, at-risk, reports |
  

  
Your team gets a sandbox tenant with fake patients. Book, bill, prescribe, refund, break things — none of it touches real records.

We do not move to the next step until your front desk can complete a full check-in → consultation → invoice → follow-up loop unaided.
  

  
Ownership of the tenant transfers to your nominated super admin. From this point RetAI staff hold no standing access to your clinic's data — support access is time-boxed and requested in the WhatsApp group.
  

  
Every account created during setup resets its password. No credential that passed through onboarding remains valid.
  

  
We connect your WhatsApp Business number and verify:

- Inbound patient messages arrive in the inbox and attach to the right patient
- Aisha replies correctly and books into real free slots
- Reminders, follow-ups, and invoice delivery all send
- The number is verified with the correct display name

Full detail: [Connect WhatsApp](#doc-admin/integrations/whatsapp).
  

  
Your clinic starts running on RetAI: scheduling, patient records, billing, and patient communication. Our engineer is in the WhatsApp group throughout the first day.


> **Warning:** 
Keep your previous system readable — not writable — for 30 days. Nobody should be entering data in two places, but you want the old records available while your team builds muscle memory.


  

  
The WhatsApp group stays open. Response commitments are in the [SLA](#doc-security/sla). Product updates land in the [changelog](#doc-help/changelog).
  


## What we need from you


  

### One decision-maker
A single person who can approve the service list, prices, and permissions. Rollouts stall on committees.


  

### Your patient data, once
In any format. The sooner it arrives, the sooner at-risk scoring has history to work with.


  

### A WhatsApp Business number
Either a new number or your existing clinic number, provided it is not already bound to the WhatsApp consumer app.


  

### Two hours of your team's time
Split across the two training sessions. Practice time is self-paced.

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.description: From first sign-in to your first AI-sent reminder in about 15 minutes.
quickstart.content:
This is the fastest path from an empty RetAI account to a working clinic. It assumes your account has already been created for you — see the [onboarding plan](#doc-onboarding) if it has not.


> **Note:** 
  You need **Owner** access for steps 2–5. A receptionist or doctor account can complete steps 1, 6, and 7 only.




  
Open [www.retai.tech](https://www.retai.tech) and sign in with your work email.

Two methods work:

- **Google** — one tap, recommended. Your Google account must already be registered as a staff member; RetAI never lets an unrecognised Google account create itself an account.
- **Email and password** — issued to you during onboarding.


> **Warning:** 
If sign-in says your account is not recognised, your staff record has not been created yet. Contact your clinic owner — this is a permissions issue, not a password issue.


  

  
Go to **CRM → Staff**. Add every person who will use RetAI, with the right role:

| Role | Sees by default |
| --- | --- |
| Owner | Everything. Cannot be restricted. |
| Doctor | Everything except Staff management |
| Receptionist | Calendar, patients, leads, packages, gallery, WhatsApp — not billing, inventory, or prescriptions |

You can override any of these per clinic. See [Roles & permissions](#doc-admin/roles-and-permissions).


Go to **CRM → Services**. Each service needs a name, a price, a GST rate, and a duration.

Duration matters more than it looks: it is what the AI uses to find a real free slot when a patient asks for an appointment. A service with the wrong duration produces double-booked chairs.


> **Tip:** 
Bulk-loading a long price list? Send it to us as a spreadsheet during onboarding and we import it for you — see [Data import](#doc-admin/data-import).


  

  
Patients can arrive three ways:


Send us a CSV with name, phone, email, last visit date, and treatment history. We normalise the phone numbers to E.164 and match duplicates before anything is written. Details in [Data import](#doc-admin/data-import).

The first time an unknown number messages your WhatsApp line, RetAI creates a patient record for it automatically.

**Patients → Add patient**. Fine for walk-ins.



> **Warning:** 
Phone numbers are the join key between WhatsApp, your patient list, and the message log. A number stored as `98765 43210` instead of `+919876543210` will not match an inbound WhatsApp message, and the patient will silently appear as a stranger. The importer fixes this; manual entry does not always.


  

  
This is the step that turns RetAI from a database into a retention engine. Follow [Connect WhatsApp](#doc-admin/integrations/whatsapp).

Once connected:

- Inbound patient messages land in the [WhatsApp Inbox](#doc-features/chats)
- Aisha replies, answers questions about your treatments, and books appointments
- Appointment reminders and follow-ups send themselves
- Invoices can be delivered to the patient as a PDF link
  

  
Open the [AI Calendar](#doc-features/calendar) and create an appointment for a real patient tomorrow.

Watch what happens automatically:

1. A reminder is queued for the right time before the slot
2. If Google Calendar is connected, the event appears on the clinician's calendar
3. The patient's record shows the upcoming visit


Open **At-Risk Patients**, pick the patient at the top of the list, and click **Draft message**.

RetAI writes a message grounded in that patient's actual history — the treatment they had, how long it has been, what they were part-way through. Read it, edit it if you want, and send.


That is the whole loop: RetAI notices the patient drifting, writes the message, sends it, handles the reply, and books the slot.
  


## What to do next


  

### [A day at the front desk](#doc-workflows/front-desk-day)
The full daily routine, in order.


  

### [Sell and track a package](#doc-workflows/sell-and-track-a-package)
Session allocation and GST on amount received.


  

### [Connect Google Calendar](#doc-admin/integrations/google-calendar)
Two-way sync with your clinicians' existing calendars.


  

### [Turn on the voice receptionist](#doc-admin/integrations/voice)
Catch the calls your front desk misses.

security/access-control.title: Access control
security/access-control.description: Authentication, session behaviour, de-provisioning, and the audit trail.
security/access-control.content:
## Authentication


  

### Google sign-in
Identity verified by Google, then matched to an existing staff record. **No self-registration** — an unrecognised Google account is rejected, not enrolled.


  

### Email and password
Rate-limited per IP address to blunt credential stuffing.




Sessions are signed tokens with an **8-hour idle lifetime**, refreshed on activity.

## Continuous authorisation

A session is not a permanent grant. Role and clinic are re-read from the staff record periodically rather than trusted from the token for its full lifetime.


> **Warning:** 
  Consequences worth knowing:

  - A **deactivated** staff member loses access within minutes, not at token expiry
  - A **role change** takes effect within minutes without forcing a sign-out
  - A **missing staff record grants nothing.** The failure mode is closed.



## Module-level authorisation

Every dashboard screen checks access **on the server as its first action**. Navigating directly to a module URL you lack access to returns nothing — the gating is not client-side hiding.

The set of guarded routes is verified structurally: a test suite sweeps every API route and every page for its authentication guard and clinic scoping, so **adding a route that forgets either one fails the build**.

## Tenant scoping

Clinic identity comes from the authenticated session, never from user input. See [Architecture](#doc-security/architecture).

## Rate limiting

Applied to the interfaces where abuse would be expensive or damaging:

| Interface | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Sign-in | Credential stuffing |
| AI generation | Cost and abuse |
| WhatsApp send | Number reputation |
| Inbound WhatsApp, per phone | A malfunctioning or hostile sender |
| Voice calls | Runaway outbound loops |


> **Note:** 
  Rate limiting is per running instance rather than globally coordinated. The effective ceiling scales with the number of instances. It is abuse protection, not a hard billing cap — stated because a vague claim here would be misleading.



## Audit logging

Logged with staff identity, timestamp, and the affected record:

- Sign-ins and failed sign-in attempts
- Permission and role changes
- Staff activation and deactivation
- Patient record creation, edit, and deletion
- Consultation and prescription creation and amendment
- Invoice issue, amendment, refund, and cancellation
- Discounts granted
- Inventory adjustments and wastage, with reasons
- Data exports, including full-clinic exports
- Photo exports and collection additions

Audit entries are retained independently of the records they describe. **Deleting a patient does not delete the record that the patient was deleted**, or by whom.

## Support access

RetAI staff hold no standing access to your clinic's data after handover. Support access is requested, time-boxed, and logged.


> **Tip:** 
  Ask for that log any time. If a vendor cannot tell you exactly when their own staff accessed your patient data, that is the answer to a different and more important question.



## What you should do


  
Anyone left? Deactivate them. Anyone changed role? Update it. Five minutes at month-end.
  
  
It removes the shared-password failure mode, which is the most common real-world breach path in small clinics.
  
  
A shared front-desk login makes the audit trail useless. Named accounts cost nothing.
  
  
Fewer people with refund and discount permission is a materially lower fraud surface.

security/architecture.title: Architecture
security/architecture.description: How tenant isolation, authentication, and authorisation are actually implemented.
security/architecture.content:
Written for the technically minded evaluator — a clinic's IT advisor, a group's security reviewer, or a developer integrating with the API.

## Request path

```mermaid
flowchart TD
A[Request] --> B{Session present?}
B -->|no, API| C[401 JSON]
B -->|no, page| D[Redirect to sign-in]
B -->|yes| E{Valid current staff record?}
E -->|no| C
E -->|yes| F{Role permitted this module?}
F -->|no| G[Refused]
F -->|yes| H[Scope query to clinic from session]
H --> I[Database, RLS enabled]
```

Four independent layers, in the order a request meets them:

| Layer | Decides |
| --- | --- |
| Edge | Is there a session at all? |
| Identity | Is this a valid, currently-active staff member? |
| Module access | May this role open this screen? |
| Tenant scope | Which clinic's rows may this query touch? |

## Authentication

Sessions are signed JWTs with an **8-hour idle lifetime**, refreshed on activity.

Two sign-in paths:

- **Google** — the identity is verified by Google, then matched against an existing staff record. There is no self-registration: an unrecognised Google account is rejected outright rather than creating an account.
- **Email and password** — rate-limited per IP address.

Role and clinic are re-read from the staff record periodically rather than trusted from the token for its full lifetime. This is what makes de-provisioning take effect in minutes. **A missing staff record grants nothing** — the failure mode is closed, not open.

## Tenant isolation

The single most important property in the system.

Every table carries a clinic identifier. Every query is scoped to the clinic derived from the authenticated session. Two specific implementation choices matter:


> **Warning:** 
  **Clinic identity is never read from user input.** Not from a URL parameter, not from a request body, not from a webhook payload, not from AI output. It comes from the session, or from a server-side lookup on a verified phone number. Editing an ID in a request cannot reach another clinic's data because the ID in the request is not what the query uses.




> **Warning:** 
  **An unscoped query throws rather than returning everything.** The scoping helper raises an error if it cannot determine a clinic, and writes are refused before they run. A coding mistake that forgets scoping produces a failure, not a leak.



Row-level security is enabled independently on every table holding customer data. Its job is to make a leaked database credential worthless — a second layer that does not depend on the first being correct.

## Structural test coverage

Tenant scoping is not only reviewed, it is tested structurally. A test suite sweeps every API route and every dashboard page for the presence of its authentication guard and session-derived clinic scope. **Adding a route that forgets either one fails the build.**

That is a stronger guarantee than a code-review checklist, because it does not depend on a reviewer noticing.

## Webhook authentication

Public endpoints exist — inbound WhatsApp, voice events, scheduled jobs — and each authenticates itself:

| Endpoint | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| WhatsApp inbound | Cryptographic signature over the request URL and parameters |
| Voice events | Shared secret, **fails closed in production** if unconfigured |
| Scheduled jobs | Secret compared in constant time |
| Calendar OAuth callback | Signed, 10-minute-lifetime authorisation state |

Public endpoints are matched **exactly**, never by prefix. This is deliberate: a prefix rule that made the inbound WhatsApp webhook public would also make the send and inbox endpoints public.

## Idempotency

Two places where a duplicate would be visible to a patient are protected at the database level, not in application logic:

- **Inbound messages** — a uniqueness constraint on the provider's message ID. A retried webhook cannot produce a second AI reply.
- **Voice call records** — a uniqueness constraint on the provider's call ID. A retried event cannot produce a duplicate call.

Outbound messages are claimed atomically before sending, so overlapping workers cannot double-message a patient. Where delivery succeeds but bookkeeping fails, the record is parked for manual reconciliation rather than retried — a duplicate message to a patient is treated as worse than a missing log line.

## AI boundary

The model sits inside the request path, never outside the authorisation boundary:

1. The sender is cryptographically verified by the webhook signature
2. Clinic and patient are resolved server-side from that verified sender
3. Only then is the model called, with an allowlisted subset of patient fields
4. The model may choose *which action* to take; it never supplies *whose data* the action runs against
5. Outputs pass a claims filter before delivery


> **Note:** 
  Put precisely: a prompt injection can choose which tool runs. It cannot choose whose record it runs against.



## Infrastructure

| Component | Provider |
| --- | --- |
| Application hosting | Vercel |
| Database and storage | Supabase (PostgreSQL) |
| WhatsApp delivery | Twilio, over the Meta WhatsApp Business Platform |
| AI language processing | Google Gemini |
| Voice | Bolna |
| Push notifications | Firebase Cloud Messaging |

Full disclosure including data categories and processing locations: [Subprocessors](#doc-security/subprocessors).

## Known limitations

We publish these rather than waiting to be asked:

1. **Invoice creation is not a single atomic transaction.** A failure mid-write can leave a partially built invoice. Logged and reconcilable.
2. **Rate limiting is per-instance.** The effective ceiling scales with running instances. Abuse protection, not a hard cap.
3. **Backups age out on rotation.** Data deleted from primary storage persists in encrypted backups until they rotate. See [Retention & deletion](#doc-security/retention-and-deletion).

security/data-protection.title: Data protection
security/data-protection.description: Encryption, consent, clinical images, call recordings, and cross-border processing.
security/data-protection.content:
## Encryption

| Data | Protection |
| --- | --- |
| In transit | TLS on every connection — browser, mobile app, API, and every vendor interface |
| At rest | Encrypted at the storage layer, including database, images, and call recordings |
| Google refresh tokens | Additionally encrypted with **AES-256-GCM**, under a key held separately from the application session secret |
| Backups | Encrypted |


> **Note:** 
  The Google token key is deliberately separate from the session secret. Rotating one does not invalidate the other — a security operation on sessions should not silently break every clinic's calendar sync.



## Clinical images

Before-and-after photographs are the most sensitive category RetAI holds.


  

### Consent is structural
Clinical-record consent and marketing consent are recorded separately. A photo without marketing consent is **incapable** of entering a shareable collection — the export path refuses it, rather than relying on someone remembering.


  

### Signed, expiring URLs
Images are served only through short-lived signed URLs to authenticated staff. A URL copied out of the browser expires and cannot be forwarded as a permanent link.


  

### Identity masking
Where marketing consent covers the treatment area but not facial identity, masking is required before an export completes.


  

### Watermarking
Your clinic logo is applied to exports at a configured position and opacity.




## Call recordings

Recorded only where voice is enabled. A configurable consent announcement plays at call start.


> **Warning:** 
  The announcement wording is the clinic's legal responsibility. It must match what your jurisdiction requires for recording a call. Have it reviewed before go-live.



Recordings are encrypted at rest, scoped to your clinic, and deleted automatically at your configured retention period.

## Push notifications

Payloads never contain patient names or message content. A notification says a message arrived; the app loads the content afterwards under the recipient's authenticated session. A notification visible on a lock screen discloses nothing.

## Message content and AI processing

Patient message content is sent to Google Gemini for reply generation. Understand what that means:

- Only an **allowlisted subset** of patient fields accompanies the message — not the full record
- The clinic and patient are already resolved before the model is called
- Every AI decision is logged with the context it was given, so what the AI was told is auditable
- Processing occurs in the United States. Disclosed in [Subprocessors](#doc-security/subprocessors).

## Cross-border processing

Several subprocessors operate outside India. This is disclosed rather than buried:

| Vendor | Role | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vercel | Application hosting | United States, global edge |
| Supabase | Database and storage | Region selected at project setup |
| Twilio | WhatsApp delivery | United States |
| Meta | WhatsApp network | United States |
| Google | AI processing, Calendar, Sign-In | United States |
| Bolna | Voice | Confirm current region |
| Firebase | Push (device token only) | United States |

The DPDP Act permits cross-border transfer except to countries restricted by government notification. Full detail: [Subprocessors](#doc-security/subprocessors).

## Patient rights

Under India's DPDP Act, patients may access, correct, and request erasure of their data. RetAI provides the mechanisms; the **clinic is the Data Fiduciary** and decides each request.

| Right | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Access | Patient → Actions → Download summary, or Export full record |
| Correction | Edit the patient record; changes are audited |
| Erasure | Delete the patient record, subject to medical-record retention law |
| Withdraw marketing consent | Toggle on the patient record; photos immediately become unusable for marketing |
| Stop messages | Opt-out, honoured permanently and immediately |


> **Warning:** 
  Erasure is not unconditional. Medical-record retention obligations under Indian law may require you to keep clinical records for a minimum period regardless of a patient's request. That assessment is the clinic's to make, with its own legal advice — RetAI does not make it for you.



## Staff device security

RetAI stores no local copy of patient data on staff devices. The mobile app is a thin authenticated shell around the same secure application the web serves.

A lost phone is a session to revoke, not a database to recover. Deactivating and reactivating the staff account invalidates it.

## Related


  

### [DPDP compliance](#doc-security/dpdp)
Roles and obligations under Indian law.


  

### [Retention & deletion](#doc-security/retention-and-deletion)
How long data is kept, and what deletion actually does.

security/dpdp.title: DPDP compliance
security/dpdp.description: Roles, consent, patient rights, and what the clinic is responsible for under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
security/dpdp.content:
> **Warning:** 
  This page explains how RetAI is built to support DPDP compliance. It is not legal advice. Your clinic is the Data Fiduciary and remains responsible for its own compliance. Take advice from a qualified Indian lawyer on your specific obligations.



## Who is who

| Role | Who | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Data Principal** | Your patient | Holds the rights |
| **Data Fiduciary** | **Your clinic** | Decides why and how patient data is processed. Answerable for consent, notice, and rights requests. |
| **Data Processor** | RetAI | Processes on your documented instructions. Provides the mechanisms; does not decide the purposes. |


> **Note:** 
  This distinction is the one clinics get wrong. RetAI is your processor, not your compliance department. We give you consent capture, audit, export, and deletion — you decide what you collect, why, and what you tell patients.



## Consent

RetAI records consent as discrete, separately-recorded permissions rather than a single blanket agreement:

| Consent | Captured | Effect if absent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Treatment and clinical records | At registration | Cannot proceed |
| WhatsApp communication | At registration or first contact | No automated messages sent |
| Marketing use of photographs | Per photo, explicitly | Photo **structurally barred** from any shareable collection |
| Call recording | Announced at call start | Configure per your legal advice |
| Marketing communication | Separate from service communication | No promotional messages |

Consent state is visible on the patient record and every consent change is audited.


> **Warning:** 
  **Marketing consent on photographs is not a display toggle.** A photo without it cannot be added to a shareable collection at all — the export path refuses it and states why. Under DPDP, "we forgot to blur it" is not a defence, so we made the failure impossible rather than unlikely.



## Patient rights, and how to satisfy each

| Right | In RetAI |
| --- | --- |
| **Access** | Patient → Actions → Download summary (PDF), or Export full record (JSON plus images) |
| **Correction** | Edit the patient record. Changes are audited. |
| **Erasure** | Delete the patient record, subject to retention law below |
| **Withdraw consent** | Toggle on the patient record. Photos immediately become unusable for marketing. |
| **Grievance redressal** | Your clinic must publish a contact. RetAI supports you on anything requiring platform action. |


> **Warning:** 
  **Erasure is not unconditional.** Medical-record retention obligations under other Indian law may require you to retain clinical records for a minimum period regardless of an erasure request. That assessment is the clinic's, with its own legal advice. RetAI will action your instruction; it will not make the judgement for you.



## Notice

As Data Fiduciary you must tell patients what you collect, why, who it is shared with, and how to exercise their rights. A patient-notice template is provided during [onboarding](#doc-onboarding) as a starting point — **have it reviewed by your lawyer before using it.**

## Cross-border transfer

Several RetAI subprocessors operate outside India. The DPDP Act permits cross-border transfer except to countries restricted by government notification.

Every subprocessor, what it processes, and where, is listed in [Subprocessors](#doc-security/subprocessors). Clinics are notified at least **15 days** before a new subprocessor is engaged, and may object on reasonable data-protection grounds.

## Breach notification

If a personal data breach affects your clinic's data, RetAI notifies you without undue delay with what is known: what happened, what data was affected, what we have done, and what you should do. As Data Fiduciary, notification to the Data Protection Board and to affected patients is your obligation; we provide what you need to make it.

See [Incident response](#doc-security/incident-response).

## Data Processing Agreement

A DPA is executed with every clinic, covering processing scope, subprocessor notification, security measures, breach notification, and deletion on termination. Ask your account contact for the current version.

## What we support versus what you own


  

### RetAI provides
Consent capture and audit, access and portability exports, correction with audit, deletion mechanisms, retention scheduling, breach notification to you, subprocessor disclosure, and a DPA.


  

### Your clinic owns
Deciding what you collect and why, patient notice, evaluating erasure requests against retention law, publishing a grievance contact, staff training, and your own legal advice.

security/incident-response.title: Incident response
security/incident-response.description: What happens if something goes wrong, and what we commit to telling you.
security/incident-response.content:
## Reporting


  

### Security vulnerability
**security@retai.tech** — acknowledged within one business day.


  

### Suspected data incident affecting your clinic
Your clinic WhatsApp group, or **security@retai.tech**. Treated as Critical.




## Responsible disclosure

We will not pursue legal action against good-faith security research that avoids privacy violations, data destruction, and service disruption.


> **Warning:** 
  Please do not test against a live clinic tenant — real patient data is involved. Ask us for a test tenant and we will provide one.



## Our process


  
From monitoring, a customer report, or a researcher. Severity assigned within one hour of a credible report.
  
  
Stop the bleeding first — revoke credentials, disable an affected path, block an origin. Containment precedes root-cause analysis.
  
  
What data was affected, whose, over what window, and whether it was actually accessed rather than merely accessible. The distinction matters and we will state which one we can evidence.
  
  
Affected clinics are notified without undue delay with what is known at that point — including when the picture is still incomplete. We do not wait for a complete account before telling you something happened.
  
  
Fix the root cause, not only the symptom. Where a structural test can prevent recurrence, we add one.
  
  
A written post-incident report to affected clinics: what happened, why, what data was involved, what we did, and what changed so it cannot recur the same way.
  


## What we commit to telling you

If a personal data breach affects your clinic's data, you receive:

- The nature of the breach and the categories of data involved
- Approximate number of records affected
- The window during which data was exposed
- Whether we can evidence actual access, or only potential access
- What we have done, and what you should do
- A named contact for follow-up


> **Note:** 
  As **Data Fiduciary**, notification to the Data Protection Board and to affected patients is your clinic's obligation. Our job is to give you everything you need to make that notification accurately and quickly. See [DPDP compliance](#doc-security/dpdp).



## Our own history of disclosure

We publish material security findings from our own audits rather than only the ones someone else discovers. The [known limitations](#doc-security/architecture) section exists for that reason.


> **Tip:** 
  A vendor that has never published a limitation has either never looked or is not telling you. Ask any vendor — including us — what their last internal audit found.



## Your responsibilities


  
A staff account behaving oddly, an unexpected export, a device lost with a signed-in session. Speed matters more than certainty.
  
  
A leaver with a live account is the most common real-world incident vector in small clinics.
  
  
A full clinic export is complete patient PHI in a file. Once downloaded, its security is yours.

security/overview.title: Security overview
security/overview.description: How RetAI protects clinical data — isolation, encryption, access control, and the limits we state plainly.
security/overview.content:
> **Note:** 
  RetAI holds patient health information. This page states what we actually do, including where our protections end. A vendor security page that reads as though nothing could ever go wrong is not one you should trust.



## The four properties that matter


  

### [Clinic isolation](#doc-security/architecture)
Every record belongs to exactly one clinic. Clinic identity comes from your authenticated session, never from a URL or request body — so no request can be edited into reaching another clinic's data.


  

### [Encryption everywhere](#doc-security/data-protection)
TLS in transit, encryption at rest for all data including images and call recordings, and separately-keyed encryption for stored third-party tokens.


  

### [Access control that fails closed](#doc-security/access-control)
Module access is checked on the server on every page load. A revoked or deactivated staff member loses access within minutes, not at session expiry.


  

### [Complete audit trail](#doc-security/access-control)
Sign-ins, permission changes, record edits, discounts, refunds, and exports are all logged with staff identity and timestamp.




## Defence in depth

Isolation is enforced at two independent layers, so a failure in either one does not expose data on its own:

1. **Application layer** — every query is scoped to your clinic before it runs. Unscoped queries throw rather than returning everything.
2. **Database layer** — row-level security is enabled on every table holding customer data, so a leaked database credential does not become a data breach.

## Third-party access

Where a request touches an external service, that service is authenticated in both directions:

| Interface | Protection |
| --- | --- |
| Inbound WhatsApp webhook | Cryptographic signature verification on every request |
| Inbound voice webhook | Shared secret; **fails closed in production** when unconfigured |
| Scheduled jobs | Secret compared in constant time |
| Google Calendar authorisation | Signed, time-limited authorisation state |

## AI safety

Aisha reads patient data to do her job. Two properties bound what that can mean:


> **Warning:** 
  **The AI does not choose whose data it touches.** Clinic and patient are resolved on the server from the verified message sender before the model is involved. A crafted or malicious message can influence what the AI *says*; it cannot make the AI read or write another patient's record.



The model also receives only an allowlisted set of patient fields, not the whole record, and its outputs pass a claims filter before reaching a patient.

## What we do not claim

Stated plainly, because a vague claim is worse than an honest limit:

- **We are not HIPAA-certified** and do not currently hold Business Associate Agreements with our vendors. RetAI is built for the Indian market and the DPDP Act. If you need HIPAA coverage, we are not currently the right vendor.
- **Some processing happens outside India.** Several subprocessors operate from the United States. Every one is disclosed in [Subprocessors](#doc-security/subprocessors), which is the point of that page.
- **Rate limiting is per-instance, not global.** The effective ceiling scales with the number of running application instances. It is protection against abuse and runaway loops, not a hard billing cap.
- **Invoice writes are not a single atomic transaction.** An infrastructure failure mid-write can produce a partially built invoice. These are logged and reconcilable. See [Billing](#doc-features/billing).

## Reporting a vulnerability

Email **security@retai.tech** with steps to reproduce. We acknowledge within one business day.

We will not pursue legal action against good-faith research that avoids privacy violations, data destruction, and service disruption. Please do not test against a live clinic tenant — ask us for a test tenant and we will provide one.
