security/retention-and-deletion.title: Retention & deletion
security/retention-and-deletion.description: How long each category of data is kept, what deletion actually does, and what happens if you leave.
security/retention-and-deletion.content:
## While your subscription is active

| Data | Retention |
| --- | --- |
| Patient records, appointments, treatment plans, invoices | For the duration of your subscription, per your configuration and applicable healthcare record-keeping law |
| WhatsApp message content and call transcripts | For the duration of the subscription, unless you delete a conversation |
| Clinical images | For the duration of the subscription, or your configured image retention period if shorter |
| Call recordings | Your configured retention period, then automatically deleted |
| Staff accounts and access logs | Subscription duration plus 12 months, for security investigation |
| Audit log | Minimum 3 years, **even where the underlying record has been deleted** |


> **Note:** 
  The audit log outliving the records it describes is deliberate. Deleting a patient does not delete the record that a patient was deleted, when, and by whom. Without that, deletion itself becomes untraceable.



## When you delete something


  
Immediately. It stops appearing anywhere in the product.
  
  
For up to 30 days, until backups rotate. This is standard practice for maintaining recoverability, and it is a real property you should know about rather than one we obscure.
  
  
No further copy remains.
  
  
The deletion event itself is retained as an integrity record.
  



> **Warning:** 
  Deletion is not instantaneous everywhere. If you are actioning an erasure request under a legal deadline, the primary-storage deletion is immediate; complete purge from backups follows the rotation schedule above. Say this accurately to a patient rather than promising instant total erasure.



## Patient erasure requests

Your clinic is the Data Fiduciary and evaluates each request, including any exception — medical-record retention obligations under other Indian law may require you to keep clinical records regardless.

RetAI actions a deletion instruction from you within **15 business days**.

## If you leave RetAI


  
Your complete dataset stays available for export. Full clinic archive plus all clinical images. See [Data export](#doc-admin/data-export).
  
  
Deleted from primary storage.
  
  
Aged out of encrypted backups.
  
  
Clinic name, subscription dates, and billing history, as required for our own tax and accounting obligations under Indian law.
  



> **Tip:** 
  Export before you need to, not after. The 30-day window is generous but it is a window, and the last week of a vendor relationship is not when you want to discover you needed something.



## Backups

Encrypted, rolling, retained for disaster recovery. They are not a per-record undo — a record deleted from primary storage ages out of backups rather than being surgically removed from every copy.


> **Warning:** 
  If you delete something by accident, tell us **immediately**. Recovery from backup is possible within the rotation window but it restores to a point in time, which has consequences for everything else changed since. It is a last resort, not a routine operation.



## Configurable retention

| Setting | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Call recording retention | [Voice setup](#doc-admin/integrations/voice) |
| Clinical image retention | [Clinic setup](#doc-admin/clinic-setup) |
| Conversation deletion | Per conversation, in the [WhatsApp Inbox](#doc-features/chats) |


> **Warning:** 
  Do not set retention shorter than your medical-record obligations. A clinic that auto-deletes clinical images at 12 months may be deleting records it is legally required to hold. Confirm the period with your own legal advice before shortening it.

security/sla.title: Service levels
security/sla.description: Uptime targets, support response times, maintenance, and service credits.
security/sla.content:
> **Note:** 
  This page summarises the SLA for readability. The contractual document is the Service Level Agreement executed with your clinic; where the two differ, the executed SLA governs. Ask your account contact for the current version.



## Uptime

RetAI targets **99.5% monthly uptime** for the core application — sign-in, patient records, appointments, and billing.

## Exclusions

The uptime commitment does not cover:

| Exclusion | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Scheduled maintenance | Announced at least 24 hours ahead, capped where reasonably possible |
| Third-party outages | Downtime caused by a subprocessor outside our control. We mitigate and communicate, but cannot commit to their availability. |
| Force majeure | |
| Customer-caused issues | Your own network, API misuse, or exceeding agreed usage limits |


> **Warning:** 
  Third-party exclusion is worth understanding rather than skimming. If WhatsApp's platform has an outage, your patients cannot be messaged and no amount of RetAI availability changes that. We will tell you what is happening; we cannot fix Meta's network.



## Support response times

| Severity | Definition | Target first response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Critical** | Service completely unavailable for all users | 1 hour |
| **High** | A core feature — WhatsApp AI, billing, sign-in — broken for your clinic | 4 business hours |
| **Normal** | A non-core issue or question | 1 business day |
| **Low** | Feature request, general question | 3 business days |

Support runs during business hours IST, primarily through your clinic's WhatsApp group. See [Support](#doc-help/support).

## Service credits

If monthly uptime falls below the commitment, excluding the exclusions above:

| Monthly uptime | Credit against next month's fee |
| --- | --- |
| 99.0% – 99.5% | 5% |
| 95.0% – 99.0% | 10% |
| Below 95.0% | 25% |

Credits are the sole remedy for missed uptime and must be requested in writing within 30 days of the end of the affected month.

## Maintenance

Announced at least 24 hours ahead by email and in-app notice. Scheduled outside clinic hours wherever possible. Emergency security patches may deploy without notice; we tell you afterwards.

## Backups and recovery

Encrypted backups on a rolling schedule. Backups exist for disaster recovery, not as a per-record undo — see [Retention & deletion](#doc-security/retention-and-deletion) for what that means for deleted data.

## Status

Live status and incident history: [status.retai.tech](https://status.retai.tech). Subscribe there to be notified of incidents without waiting for us to reach you.

security/subprocessors.content:
Complete and current. A subprocessor list that omits a vendor is itself a compliance gap.


> **Note:** 
  Clinics are notified at least **15 days** before a new subprocessor is engaged, and may object on reasonable data-protection grounds. This is committed in the Data Processing Agreement.



## Current subprocessors

| Subprocessor | Role | Data processed | Location | Cross-border |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | :---: |
| **Vercel Inc.** | Application hosting | All application traffic. No direct database access. | United States, global edge | Yes |
| **Supabase Inc.** | Database and storage | All customer data — patients, appointments, invoices, messages, images, staff | Region selected at project setup | If region is outside India |
| **Twilio Inc.** | WhatsApp message delivery | Patient phone numbers; message content | United States | Yes |
| **Meta Platforms, Inc.** | WhatsApp Business Platform | Patient phone numbers; message content, as network operator | United States | Yes |
| **Google LLC** | AI processing (Gemini); Google Calendar; Google Sign-In | Message content sent for reply generation; calendar event data where connected; email and name for sign-in | United States | Yes |
| **Bolna** | AI voice calling | Patient phone numbers; call audio and transcripts, where voice is enabled | Confirm current region | Confirm |
| **Firebase (Google LLC)** | Push notifications | **Device push token only.** Notification content is generic — never a patient name or message text. | United States | Token only; no patient data |

## Notes on scope


  
It serves the application. Patient records live in the database, which Vercel does not access directly.
  
  
Only an allowlisted subset of patient fields accompanies a message to the AI. Not the full clinical record.
  
  
Push payloads carry a device token and a generic string. This is why a notification on a lock screen discloses nothing.
  
  
If your plan does not include the voice receptionist, no data reaches Bolna.
  


## Cross-border transfer

Where a subprocessor processes data outside India, this is disclosed under our Privacy Policy and DPA. The DPDP Act permits cross-border transfer except to countries restricted by government notification.

## HIPAA

  RetAI does **not** currently hold Business Associate Agreements with these vendors, and RetAI is not offered as a HIPAA-compliant product. It is built for the Indian market and the DPDP Act. If you require HIPAA coverage, we are not currently the right vendor — and we would rather say so here than in a procurement questionnaire.

workflows/consultation-to-invoice.title: Consultation to invoice
workflows/consultation-to-invoice.description: One patient, end to end — check-in, consultation, photos, prescription, package, payment, follow-up.
workflows/consultation-to-invoice.content:
The complete clinical-to-commercial loop for a single visit. Follow it once with a real patient and the product stops feeling like eleven separate screens.


  
Calendar → find the appointment → **Checked in**.

The clinician's screen now shows this patient as waiting.
  

  
From the appointment, click **Start consultation**. RetAI opens your clinic's template for that service.

Allergies and clinical flags are pinned at the top. They are not in a tab you have to remember to open.
  

  
Fill the structured fields. Where a finding is easier drawn than written, open the [annotation canvas](#doc-features/consultations), pick the base diagram — face, three-quarter, scalp, or body — and mark it.


> **Tip:** 
Number your marks. "Site 1: 0.5ml, site 2: 0.3ml" in the notes, with matching numbered markers on the diagram, is the record you will want at the review visit.


  

  
From the consultation, capture *before* images. Tag treatment, area, and angle. Record consent:

- **Clinical record** — always
- **Marketing use** — only if the patient has explicitly agreed


> **Warning:** 
If marketing consent is not given, do not tick it "to sort out later". A photo without it is structurally barred from any shareable collection, and that is the protection working. Re-consent later if the patient changes their mind.


  

  
Start from a template, adjust for the patient, sign, and issue. Deliver as PDF over WhatsApp, or print.
  

  
If the plan is a course rather than a single visit, sell it as a **package** — that is what makes session tracking, expiry reminders, and correct revenue recognition work.

If the patient needs to think about it, create a **quotation** on their lead instead and set a next-action date.
  

  
Mark today's session delivered. RetAI:

- increments sessions completed
- deducts consumables per the procedure's bill of materials
- recognises the earned portion of revenue and tax
- queues the next session's reminder
  

  
Mark it **Completed**. This queues the post-visit follow-up and any aftercare message attached to the service.
  

  
Checkout pre-fills from what was delivered. Add anything retail or pharmacy. GST computes per line at each line's own rate.

Take payment — split across methods if needed — and issue.
  

  
One click delivers the PDF to the patient's WhatsApp. It is logged on their conversation.
  

  
Before they leave the desk. This is the single highest-leverage action in the entire workflow.
  


## What happens after they walk out

Without anyone touching anything:

| When | What |
| --- | --- |
| ~1 hour after completion | Aftercare instructions sent, if configured for that service |
| A few days later | Post-visit follow-up asking how they are getting on |
| Before the next session | Appointment reminder, then a confirmation request if unconfirmed |
| If the gap grows | The patient rises on the [at-risk list](#doc-features/at-risk) with sessions remaining stated |
| As expiry approaches | Package-expiry reminder |

workflows/front-desk-day.title: A day at the front desk
workflows/front-desk-day.description: The daily routine in the order you actually do it — open, run the floor, close.
workflows/front-desk-day.content:
Written for the person at the desk. Follow it top to bottom for the first fortnight and it becomes habit.

## Opening — first 15 minutes


  
Confirm every clinician's column looks right. Anything in **Tentative** amber needs a confirmation call or message today.
  
  
Filter to **Needs attention** first — those are the threads Aisha deliberately did not answer overnight. Then work **Unread**.


> **Tip:** 
Do not read every AI-handled thread each morning. Skim the flagged ones. Reading all of them is how the inbox becomes a job instead of a tool.


  
  
Open the AI Receptionist call log filtered to overnight. Anything marked *escalated* or *callback requested* needs a human call this morning.
  
  
For each patient arriving today, glance at: outstanding balance, active package sessions remaining, and whether a photo is due this session.
  


## Running the floor


  
Find them on the calendar and mark **Checked in**. If they are new, complete the patient record — phone number with country code, always.
  

  
Nothing for you to do. The clinician writes the consultation and any prescription. If a session photograph is due, they or you capture it against the session.
  

  
In one flow:

1. Mark the appointment **Completed** — this triggers the post-visit follow-up and deducts consumables
2. Open checkout, add what was delivered
3. Take payment; split across methods if needed
4. Send the invoice over WhatsApp
5. Book the next session before they leave


> **Warning:** 
Step 5 is the one that gets skipped when the desk is busy, and it is the one that matters most. A patient who leaves without a next appointment is the patient who ends up on the at-risk list eight weeks later.


  

  
The AI Receptionist answers. Check the call log when you get a gap; anything it escalated will be flagged.
  

  
Create a **lead**, not a patient. Log what they asked about, build a quotation if they want prices, and set a next-action date before they leave.
  


## Quiet moments — the highest-value 20 minutes in the day

When the floor is calm:


  

### [Work the at-risk list](#doc-features/at-risk)
Top five rows. Draft, read, send.


  

### [Chase expiring packages](#doc-features/packages)
Filter to expiring within 30 days with sessions remaining. Already-paid patients convert fastest.


  

### [Confirm tomorrow](#doc-features/calendar)
List view for tomorrow. Confirm every tentative slot.


  

### [Follow up overdue leads](#doc-features/leads)
Anything past its next-action date and assigned to you.




## Closing — last 15 minutes


  
Collections by method against what is in the till and on the card machine. Reconcile now, while the person who took each payment is still here.
  
  
Nothing unread, nothing flagged, going into the night.
  
  
Any unconfirmed slots left? Send the confirmation request before you leave; overnight replies get handled by Aisha.
  
  
Anything running low that the automatic deduction would not catch — a broken vial, a sample given away. Record it as wastage with a reason.

workflows/month-end-close.title: Month-end close
workflows/month-end-close.description: The owner's monthly routine — reconcile, report, review retention, and hand your accountant a clean file.
workflows/month-end-close.content:
About forty minutes on the first working day of the month.

## 1 — Reconcile the money


  
Reports → Day-end, filtered to last month. A missing day means a day nobody reconciled. Find it now, not in the audit.
  
  
Collected versus billed for the month. Split by payment method and reconcile against bank and card settlements.
  
  
Anything past 30 days gets a call this week. Sort by amount.
  
  
Both are liabilities. Rising advance balances mean you are collecting faster than you are delivering — good for cash, but it is treatment you owe.
  


## 2 — Tax


  
Tax collected by rate with taxable value per rate. Export to CSV.
  
  
Package revenue should appear as earned, not as collected. Unearned advance is not this month's taxable revenue.
  
  
Each with its reason and the staff member who authorised it.
  
  
[Data export](#doc-admin/data-export) produces invoices, line items, payments, and the tax breakdown in one archive.
  


## 3 — Review retention

This is the section that changes what you do next month.


  

### Revenue recovered
What at-risk outreach brought back. Compare against your subscription cost.


  

### Retention rate
Share of patients returning within their expected interval, trended.


  

### Package completion
Sold sessions actually delivered. Below 70% means your allocation-at-sale discipline is slipping.


  

### No-show analysis
Cross-check against reminder delivery. Undelivered reminders are a fixable cause.




## 4 — Review operations

| Report | What you are looking for |
| --- | --- |
| Clinician utilisation | Booked against available hours. Under 60% is a marketing problem; over 90% is a capacity problem. |
| Procedure trends | What is growing, what is fading, period over period |
| Discounts granted | Discount as a share of gross, by staff member |
| Lead conversion | By source and by owner, with lost reasons |
| Consumption by procedure | Two clinicians consuming differently for the same procedure is training or leakage |
| Stock value and wastage | Write-offs and expiry losses |

## 5 — Housekeeping


  
Physical count against system quantities. Post adjustments with the stock-take reference.
  
  
Anyone left? Deactivate them. Anyone changed role? Update their modules.
  
  
Changing prices affects future invoices only. Existing packages hold their agreed price.
  
  
Read ten AI-handled WhatsApp threads and five voice transcripts. You are checking tone and accuracy, not policing. Anything wrong is usually a service description that needs rewording.
  


## 6 — Set next month's push

Pick one number to move and one action to move it. Examples that work:

- *Package completion below 70%* → allocate every session at the point of sale, without exception
- *No-shows above 12%* → move the reminder from 24h to 24h **and** 2h
- *Utilisation under 60% on Tuesdays* → run a targeted at-risk campaign filtered to Tuesday-preferring patients

workflows/sell-and-track-a-package.title: Sell and track a package
workflows/sell-and-track-a-package.description: Quotation to sale to session delivery to expiry recovery — including how the money is recognised.
workflows/sell-and-track-a-package.content:
Packages are where most aesthetic revenue lives and where most clinic accounting goes wrong. This walkthrough covers both the clicks and the arithmetic.

## 1 — Quote it


  
If they are already a patient, quote from the patient record instead.
  
  
Add the package, apply any discount the counsellor is authorised to give. GST computes per line at each line's own rate.
  
  
Branded PDF over WhatsApp. Set a next-action date on the lead before you close the screen.
  


## 2 — Sell it

Convert the accepted quotation straight to checkout — nothing is retyped, so the quoted price and the billed price cannot drift apart.

At checkout, four numbers are tracked separately. Conflating them is the classic error:

| Term | Example |
| --- | --- |
| **List price** | ₹60,000 for 6 laser sessions |
| **Discount** | ₹6,000 granted by the counsellor |
| **Agreed price** | ₹54,000 — what the patient owes |
| **Amount received** | ₹20,000 paid today |

RetAI then derives:

- **Outstanding** — ₹34,000 still to collect
- **Per-session value** — ₹9,000
- **Earned value** — ₹0 today; no session has been delivered
- **Unearned advance** — ₹20,000, a *liability*. You have taken money and owe treatment for it.


> **Note:** 
  This is the point of the module. A six-session package sold today is not six sessions of revenue today, and not six sessions of GST liability today.



## 3 — Allocate the sessions


RetAI proposes dates from the package's configured session interval. Adjust anything, then confirm. Each becomes a real appointment with its own reminder.


> **Tip:** 
  Allocate all sessions at the point of sale, even if dates shift later. A package with sessions on the calendar completes far more often than one the patient is expected to remember to book.



## 4 — Deliver a session

Marking session 1 delivered:

1. Sessions completed → 1, remaining → 5
2. Earned value → ₹9,000; unearned advance → ₹11,000
3. GST recognised on the earned portion, at the correct per-line rate
4. Consumables deducted from stock via the bill of materials
5. Session photograph prompted, bound to session 1
6. Session 2's reminder queued


### When delivery runs ahead of collection

If you deliver session 3 while only ₹20,000 has been collected, earned value (₹27,000) exceeds amount received. RetAI shows that as **delivered unpaid: ₹7,000** — treatment given away pending collection.


> **Warning:** 
  Delivered-unpaid is the number that quietly grows in clinics without package accounting. Check it on the package report weekly, not at year end.



## 5 — Recover the remainder

RetAI chases sessions without anyone remembering to:

| Trigger | What is sent |
| --- | --- |
| Session interval exceeded | Reminder that the next session is due |
| Package expiry in 30 days with sessions remaining | Expiry reminder |
| Gap widening beyond the patient's own rhythm | Patient rises on the [at-risk list](#doc-features/at-risk) with sessions-remaining stated in the draft |

## 6 — Close it out


  
Package marked complete. Full agreed price recognised. It stays on the patient record as history.
  
  
Flagged on the package report. Your policy decides — extend, part-refund, or forfeit. Whatever you choose is recorded with a reason.
  
  
Refundable amount computes as amount received minus earned value, adjusted per your policy. Recorded against the original invoice so the audit trail holds.

workflows/win-back-a-lapsed-patient.title: Win back a lapsed patient
workflows/win-back-a-lapsed-patient.description: From at-risk row to booked appointment, with the AI doing most of the work.
workflows/win-back-a-lapsed-patient.content:
This is the workflow RetAI exists for. It takes about ninety seconds per patient.


  
Sorted by **revenue at stake**, not by days absent. The top row is the most valuable call available to you today.


Every row states why it is there, in plain terms:

> *3 of 6 laser sessions remaining · 9 weeks since last visit · package expires in 41 days · ₹18,400 at stake*

You are never guessing what to say.
  

  
Click **Draft message**. RetAI writes it from that patient's own history — the treatment, the gap, what is unfinished, what expires when.


You always see the draft. Edit anything. The model will not promise results, invent an offer, or make a clinical claim — but your judgement about tone is still better than its own.


> **Tip:** 
Shorter converts better. If the draft is four sentences, cut it to two. The goal is a reply, not a pitch.


  

  
Delivered over WhatsApp from your clinic number. Logged on the patient's conversation.
  

  
When the patient answers — often within the hour — Aisha reads the thread, answers their questions from your catalogue, offers real free slots, and books.


You are only involved if she escalates, which she does for anything clinical or any complaint.
  

  
Once the appointment exists, the patient leaves the at-risk list. The recovered value is attributed to the message that produced it and appears in **Revenue recovered** in [Reports](#doc-features/reports).
  


## Doing it in bulk

Filter the list — *"package expiring within 30 days, sessions remaining"* — and send to everyone matching. Each message is written per patient from their own history; this is not a mail merge.


> **Warning:** 
  Bulk sends are rate-limited and spread over time. That is protecting your number: a hundred near-identical messages inside a minute is how a WhatsApp Business number gets restricted.



## If they do not reply


  
The patient reappears on the at-risk list with the previous attempt noted. Send a second, differently-framed message — the draft accounts for the first attempt.
  
  
Escalate to voice. Trigger an outbound call from the patient record, or call them yourself. A high-value patient with unredeemed sessions deserves a human.
  
  
Mark them dormant. They stop appearing in the daily list but stay in reporting, and a future visit reactivates them automatically.
  


## Measuring it

[Reports → Revenue recovered](#doc-features/reports) attributes bookings to the outreach that produced them. That number against your subscription cost is the only ROI calculation that matters.

## Related


  

### [At-Risk Patients](#doc-features/at-risk)
How the score is built.


  

### [WhatsApp Inbox](#doc-features/chats)
Where the replies arrive.
